title: Prescriptive rewrite: every chapter re-read under ADR-0032, ratchet to zero
description:
Umbrella for the review ADR-0032 started. The set became prescriptive and implementation-agnostic on 2026-09-12 (spec-repo PR #1, merge c6354f3); the rules landed there and each chapter is now re-read under them, one pull request per chapter, in dependency order.

READ FIRST, every ticket: docs/adr/0032-specification-is-prescriptive-and-implementation-agnostic.md (the decision, the refactor test, the fate of each chapter), README.md 'Requirement conventions' and 'How compliance is measured', AGENTS.md.

The refactor test: a sentence is a requirement only if a rewrite that keeps every byte on disk, every byte on the wire and every observable behaviour identical CANNOT violate it. On-disk shapes, wire shapes, protocol facts and persisted/serialized type names stay. Function and method names, crate and file paths, line numbers, frameworks, the fork pin, the actor mechanism go; their behaviours and invariants stay as requirements.

Done-condition shared by every chapter ticket:
1. Every requirement in the chapter re-read, not re-moded: states a behaviour observable at a boundary (federation/gateway, seed, frontend, durability); says what the wallet SHOULD do, so where today's code differs the requirement changes and the code gains a finding; buildable from the text alone.
2. Requirements that described only a codebase fact are withdrawn: id removed, row added to README.md 'Withdrawn identifiers' (Identifier | Was | Why it went). Never renumber, never reuse.
3. New behaviour a re-read exposes gets the next free id in its namespace.
4. tools/codebase-refs-baseline.txt: the chapter's line lowered to its new count (target 0) in the same PR.
5. bash tools/check-all.sh exit 0, run unpiped, before and after.
6. The PR description carries a HAND-OFF LIST for the code repository: each Fn in douglaz/fedimint-wallets/docs/open-findings.md whose sense changes (gap-vs-decision becomes non-conformance-vs-requirement), each new non-conformance a strengthened requirement creates, and each finding a withdrawn requirement orphans. A code-repo bead is cut from that list when the PR merges; it is not this ticket's work.
7. One PR per chapter; the two review bots run on every push; address findings, then merge.

Order (blocking edges): 00 → 01 → 02 → 03 → 05 → 06 → 04 → 07 → 08 → 09 → 10 → final pass. Persistence before allocator because ALC cites STO properties; API after the lifecycle because 04 is the wire view of 03.

title: Chapter 02 fedimint integration: rewrite under ADR-0032 (fork pin out, patched behaviours in)
description:
Rewrite 02-fedimint-integration.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 35 lines — second heaviest. This chapter is where 'environment vs codebase' bites: the Fedimint federation and gateway protocols are presupposed and cited freely; the SDK's internal API is not.
Decided in ADR-0032:
- FMI-1 (the douglaz/fedimint fork pin at a revision) and FMI-2 (any repoint carries every patch) GO. Each behaviour the three patches provide becomes its own FMI requirement: iroh long-poll bound, recovery complete-or-fail, single-share TPE correctness. Hand-off: F19 (the pin) becomes 'satisfied by fork patch, not upstream' compliance notes on those requirements; F20 (lnv2 claim-retry / reclaim_receive) is a non-conformance against a new requirement that a Stranded move has a recovery path — write that requirement.
- FMI-7 seed derivation STAYS and becomes normative with the derivation stated, no SDK names: two implementations must derive the same keys or recovery is not implementation-independent.
- FMI-11 keeps the routing_info exchange (protocol) and loses 'pooled HTTP client'; F45 (SSRF egress) is a non-conformance against a new SEC/FMI requirement restricting egress — coordinate with the 07 ticket, decide the owner here and cite from 07.
- FMI-13 gateway_serves_route(to, from, gw), FMI-36 MultiClient::new/ConnectorRegistry, FMI-3 'four modules on one ClientBuilder' — restate as behaviour (which modules a joined federation must expose; how transport is decided by invite and config).
- FMI-10 'the SDK's list_gateways(None)' — the vetted list is defined by ADR-0029 (threshold-vetted, read per guardian); write the requirement to the ADR, F6 becomes the non-conformance.
- FMI-19 'enforced at the pin, on the wrong ordering' — descriptive of a defect; the requirement is the correct ordering (component-wise), the current behaviour is a finding.
Hand-off: F6, F19, F20, F45 change sense; possibly new findings for FMI-19.

title: Chapter 03 operation lifecycle: rewrite under ADR-0032 (invariants stay, actor goes)
description:
Rewrite 03-operation-lifecycle.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 22 lines. The chapter's substance — admission, execution, resumption, terminalization, the four killpoints, supersession, reconcile — is behaviour and stays. What goes is the mechanism: 'through the actor', 'Runtime::tick', 'Runtime::do_move', 'the standalone path bypasses the actor' (OPS-12, OPS-5 etc). Per ADR-0032 the invariants are requirements: one serialized admission point; one live key per allocator goal; agent work admitted nowhere else; generation-fenced writes; no operation's network IO on the admission point. State them as MUSTs on the wallet, not on an actor.
The standalone tick admission exception (ADR-0031, CONTEXT.md Engine) is behaviour and stays.
OPS-39 (RefuseReason by message substring) is a wire contract nobody documented as one — under the prescriptive posture decide: either the reason codes are the contract (write the table as normative, message text informative) or the substrings are; recommend codes. Hand-off: F37 changes sense.
F42 (standalone probe bypasses actor) and F44 (user move attaches to a probe leg) are non-conformances against the admission invariants once written; F8 (refused-after-commit row on the planned pair) against the ledger-correctness requirement — say which requirement each violates in the hand-off.

title: Chapter 05 persistence: rewrite under ADR-0032 (on-disk shapes stay, write paths go)
description:
Rewrite 05-persistence.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 43 lines — the heaviest chapter, and the one where the refactor test does the most work. ON DISK STAYS: two stores (STO-1), the advisory lock file (STO-2), partition prefixes (STO-3), the seed encoding (STO-4), key tags and value encodings (STO-5), correlation/idempotency key shapes (STO-6), every persisted row field by field (STO-9..15, 26), the serde-rules-as-encoding (STO-29..31: a field added to a persisted type MUST decode when absent; no persisted type rejects unknown fields). These are an upgrade-in-place contract.
GOES: 'enforced by the pure advance function' (STO-16), 'repair_ledger scans' (STO-24), wallet_core::MoveRecord paths, 'fedimint's raw byte transactions' as mechanism (STO-7 — keep the atomicity property), which writer performs a write. Keep every PROPERTY: write discipline, CAS fencing (STO-8), O(1) sequence assignment (STO-18), one current row per correlation key (STO-20), the Agent occurrence floor (STO-21..23), unreadable rows never fence automation (STO-22), terminal immutability, the OPS-24 ordering.
STO-32 ('greenfield in one respect... unverified against the long-running deployment's store') is deployment content: the requirement is that the two fields decode when absent like every other; F38 is the check against one store and stays a code-repo item. STO-19 'full ascending scan, reverses' is an algorithm — keep the observable (history is newest-first, paged by before_seq), drop the scan.
Hand-off: F12 (no app-state backup) — decide whether a snapshot/restore is a requirement (ADR-0025 says the seed is the backup unit; Restore is an operator action) or stays a code-repo task; F38, F41 sense; F7 (committed route not persisted) is a non-conformance against the Committed route requirement (cite ADR-0030).
See the epic for the shared done-condition.

title: Chapter 06 allocator and automation: rewrite under ADR-0032
description:
Rewrite 06-allocator-and-automation.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 22 lines. The decision core is already stated as a pure function over a snapshot — keep that as a requirement (determinism, no IO) without naming decide(). Route economics, scoring, probes, discovery, evacuation, the tick, the scheduler cycle and the readiness signal are behaviour.
Watch for: ALC-15 'unreachable in production' (the scorer's activity buckets) — a prescriptive set does not carry dead branches; either the buckets are required behaviour with a stated input, or the requirement is withdrawn. ALC-19 (two evacuation leads with one name) — decide the requirement: one lead, or two with distinct names; F36 becomes the non-conformance. ALC-45..49 (readiness, the fourth invisible suppression, eight fail-closed paths without a ledger row, the light probe four times per cycle) are currently written as descriptions of defects: rewrite each as the requirement (every suppression reported on /v1/health; every fail-closed path leaves a row; the light probe runs once per cycle or the count is a stated requirement) and hand off F32, F33, F34 as non-conformances. 'Runtime::watch_once is a dev/test harness with no production caller' fails the refactor test — withdraw or restate as 'no host schedules through anything but the engine's cycle'. ALC-50 (cfg(test) seams) is codebase — withdraw.
The F1 shortfall-with-no-signal: requirement = every withheld funding decision is recorded (see 00 ticket); F1 non-conformance. F10 (no aggregate ceiling) — decide whether an aggregate exposure cap is a requirement (recommend yes, since exposure otherwise scales with joins) and hand off. F15 (conflict-suppressed goals not in status) likewise.
Hand-off: F1, F10, F14, F15, F32, F33, F34, F36 change sense; F3 (hop unbuilt) is a non-conformance against ADR-0029's requirements — make sure the hop requirement is written here, not only in the ADR.

title: Chapter 07 security: rewrite under ADR-0032
description:
Rewrite 07-security-requirements.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 3 lines — light on codebase refs, heavy on 'what is actually enforced — including what is not', which is the descriptive posture in its purest form. Every 'not enforced' becomes either a requirement (and a finding in the hand-off) or a decided non-goal citing its ADR.
Known items:
- The seed at rest (SEC-n citing ADR-0026). Write the requirement at the level ADR-0026 DECIDED, no further: the seed MUST NOT be stored in plaintext; it is protected by AEAD over the stored entropy under a key not stored beside it; when the key source is unavailable at start the wallet fails closed and never falls back to plaintext; mnemonic export and restore-mnemonic keep working. The KEY SOURCE (operator passphrase with a memory-hard KDF vs KMS/HSM) is a RECOMMENDATION in ADR-0026 'to ratify in the implementation bead', not a decision — do not ratify it through this rewrite. If the 07 PR wants to settle it, propose an ADR-0026 amendment in the PR and let it be accepted on its own; until then the requirement is silent on key derivation. F11 is the non-conformance.
- SEC-17 (no ADR records the per-guardian response bound) — write the bound as a requirement or withdraw the sentence.
- SEC-20 / DEF-22 (deployment identity not in tracked files) is a code-repo hygiene rule about one tree, not a wallet requirement — withdraw SEC-20 here (DEF-22 handled by the 09 ticket).
- SEC-24 (an id alone carries no guardian endpoints) stays.
- F45 egress restriction: the owner is decided by the 02 ticket; cite it from here.
Threat model: keep, as the frame the requirements answer. Remove any 'today the code does X' hedges.
Hand-off: F11, F21 (deployment identity in git history — code-repo only, no spec requirement), F45 sense.

title: Chapter 10 conformance: the normative scenario suite
description:
Rewrite 10-conformance-checklist.md as the normative scenario suite (ADR-0032). Baseline today: 11 lines. Each surviving CNF-n is a scenario — given / when / then — at the wallet's boundaries, names the requirements it demonstrates ('demonstrates: ALC-20, DEF-21'), and carries NO result: no checkbox, no commit hash, no test function name, no run date, no gate command line. Add the sentence that makes it normative: a conformant implementation MUST pass every scenario.
Scenarios are stated against the wallet's ENVIRONMENT — two federations, their gateways, a Lightning node, a crash at a named point — never against a harness. devimint is the reference implementation's harness and lives in the code repository; a scenario does not name it, any harness that produces the given state is admissible, and how the code repository realises each scenario is its conformance-results file's business.
WITHDRAW (README rows): process discipline CNF-1, CNF-2, CNF-3, CNF-30, CNF-39, CNF-40 (to the code repo's AGENTS.md — most already there); build/unit results CNF-4, CNF-5; work items wearing a CNF id: CNF-45 (human reading of four boundaries, F26), CNF-46 (sidecar, F27), CNF-47 (seed re-encryption, F11), CNF-48 (restore drill) — their Fn already track them. Every other unchecked box is either a scenario nobody has run (keep as a scenario; the code repo's results say unrun) or a finding (withdraw, hand off).
ADD scenarios the chapter rewrites exposed as missing: the flat-cap regression DEF-25 / F22 (an evacuation whose parameters discriminate the cap basis), the after-receive-commit killpoint F25, the recovery FAILURE path F24, delivered≠ask at the pre-mint gate F23. Each is a scenario here and a non-conformance ('scenario not yet runnable/passing') in the hand-off.
Verify: every requirement in 02–08 that claims to be demonstrable cites a CNF, and every CNF cites at least one requirement. Baseline to 0.

title: OPS-20 follow-up: the planned-cap fallback for an Evacuate row without fee_cap is looser than the enforced cap
description:
Raised by a review bot on spec-repo PR #7 (chapter 05) and deferred there because OPS-20 (03) owns
the precedence. OPS-20's cap precedence for reassembly is artifact > cached (only when the cache
holds a receive or send operation id) > planned. A committed receive operation whose MoveMeta
carries no `fee_cap` (a row an older build wrote; STO-33 says absent decodes as none, never zero)
therefore falls back to the intent's PLANNED cap. For an `Evacuate` the planned cap is
`fee_cap_components.at(planned amount)`, and the planned amount is larger than the delivered net,
so the reconstructed cap is LOOSER than the cap that was enforced at the sized net — the pairing
DEF-4 / STO-17 exists to prevent (an auditor recomputing the cap from an amount nobody received).

Decide, in 03: should the fallback for an `Evacuate` (an intent carrying `fee_cap_components`)
be `fee_cap_components.at(meta.amount)` — the leg's own `amount` IS on the metadata (STO-33),
so the enforced cap is reconstructible without the cache — with the planned cap only for an
action without components? Or state that such a row is not rebuildable and the pay step
re-checks under the planned cap (OPS-26 already re-quotes both legs against rec.fee_cap)?

Owner: OPS-20 (and OPS-26 if the re-check wording changes). Land as one clause; cite ADR-0029
("the cap enforced at that net") and CONTEXT.md **Delivered net**. Any code that falls back to
the planned cap today becomes a non-conformance in the code repo's open-findings.md.
Gate: bash tools/check-all.sh exit 0 before and after; 03's ratchet baseline stays 0.
close_reason: Landed in spec-repo PR #14 (e360604): OPS-20's cap fallback is the action's cap rule at the reassembled amount; OPS-25 cites it; code-repo bead br-ops20-capless-leg-fallback-nb8 tracks the implementation check

title: Review 2026-09-23: blockers and majors
description:
Umbrella for the 2026-09-23 independent review of the whole set (R1, R2, R3, R4; same prompt, read-only) and its three follow-up bead reviews. This description is the CURRENT execution contract, rewritten after review round 3 and again on 2026-10-01 after the decision session; the review history lives in review reports kept outside this repository and in git (e89d13a, 4ea6c02, c0e8e46), not here.

**Done-condition for every child** (repeat it in your head before editing; the child description is the deliverable, this is the contract): (1) the contradiction or gap is resolved in the OWNING requirement; everywhere else cites the id (README, One owner per rule); (2) a decision nobody has taken goes to 11-open-questions.md and the set stays silent (AGENTS.md); (3) a new rule gets the next free id in its namespace (verify with the gate; withdrawn ids are never reused), withdrawn ids get a README row; (4) where the requirement can be demonstrated, 10-conformance-checklist.md gains or amends the scenario and the requirement cites it back; a scenario carries no result (10:5-7); (5) `bash tools/check-all.sh` exit 0, unpiped, before and after; (6) any requirement whose sense changes for the existing implementation is listed as a hand-off for the code repository's docs/open-findings.md — this epic already owes the hand-offs listed below; (7) where a child's sections disagree, the LATEST section governs; a child marked "Rewritten … replaces every earlier version" has no earlier layers.

**Severity.** P0 = no compliant implementation can exist or funds can be lost: spec-dgj, spec-u3u, spec-cuw, spec-azs. P1 = two compliant implementations diverge observably or a scenario cannot be judged. P2 = otherwise. One reviewer (R4, and R3 in round 3) reads the rubric literally and would promote every mutually exclusive pair of sentences (1nc, 9iq, ghp, sn0, yae, euo) to P0; the majority and this epic keep them P1.

**SDK facts, verified at the code repository's pin 72b1e5be and at origin/master 57c7e8c57c5 (origin = upstream fedimint/fedimint; do not use the stale checkout under fleet-manager-specs).** The pin = upstream 5dcff669a plus three fork patches (iroh long-poll → FMI-38, recovery failure → FMI-30, single-share TPE → FMI-39). Present at the pin: single-attempt lnv2 send dedup (703a37e8f3f; `(invoice, 0)` operation id, `DuplicatePaymentAttempt`). title: SEC-25 seed encryption: implement ADR-0033 (passphrase file or unseal call, sealed state, slot-layout STO rule, CNF-47 vectors)
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-10-01: the key-source decision is taken (`ADR-0033`, docs/adr/0033-seed-key-passphrase-file-or-unseal-call.md), so this bead is no longer decision-gated. This text replaces every earlier version; read the ADR first.

**The gap (verified).** 07-security-requirements.md:101-126 (SEC-25) requires the seed under an AEAD keyed from outside the store but leaves the key source and the slot layout to a decision; 05:48-51 (STO-4) defers the same way; HST-2 (08:19-24) owns the complete environment surface and HST-3 (08:40-50) says `walletd.toml` has five keys and MUST reject any other, so no compliant channel delivers the key; HST-6 (08:97-104) has no unseal step; CNF-47 (10:288-303) needs a slot discriminator no STO rule defines.

**What ADR-0033 decided (do not re-open).** Headless hosts only (`walletd`, the standalone mode, the one-shot commands); Android keys from the Keystore (ADR-0011) and is spec-11k's. The key is an operator passphrase through a memory-hard KDF, used with an AEAD over the entropy. The passphrase arrives by a passphrase file (a new `walletd.toml` key with an `HST-2` environment override, and a standalone flag) or by an unseal call. With the file configured, start unseals from it and a missing, unreadable or wrong file fails startup (`HST-29`) — never a fallback to sealed. Without it, walletd starts SEALED: listener and token auth up; `GET /v1/health` reports a sealed flag; every other route answers one fixed 503 in API-37's shape; no store opened, no scheduler or watchdog started, until `POST /v1/unseal` (inside the token boundary, SEC-4) succeeds; a crash-restart stays sealed until the next unseal. `walletd init` requires the passphrase (file or TTY prompt) and creates the encrypted slot; there is NO API call that creates a wallet (init mints the token, so a create call would be unauthenticated). The one-shot commands take the passphrase from the file, a flag or a prompt. No plaintext-seed migration: greenfield.

**Edits.**
- SEC-25: cite ADR-0033 as the key-source decision; delete the plaintext re-encryption clause and the "silent on it" sentence; keep fail-closed, decrypt-on-demand for `mnemonic`/`restore-mnemonic`, and the rollback rule (a build that predates SEC-25 MUST fail to open the slot).
- New STO rule (next free STO; STO-32 is withdrawn — verify with the gate): the slot bytes — a version discriminator an older build cannot decode as BIP-39 entropy (BIP-39 accepts 16-32 bytes, so a bare 32-byte ciphertext would decode as a 24-word seed), the KDF and its parameters, the nonce, the ciphertext, the associated data. STO-4 cites it.
- HST-3: the passphrase-file key (do not hard-code a key count in prose other rules repeat; HST-3 owns the count). HST-2: its override variable. HST-10 and API-25: the standalone flag. HST-29: the new failure modes.
- HST-6: the serve order gains the unseal step and the sealed branch.
- API-8 route table: `POST /v1/unseal` (request: the passphrase; responses: success, wrong passphrase, not sealed). API-16: the sealed flag. API-37: the sealed 503.
- HST-4 (`init`): requires the passphrase. CONTEXT.md already defines Sealed / Unseal.
- CNF-47 restated with fixed vectors (a known passphrase and entropy produce known slot bytes) and without the migration half; its "the build that predates SEC-25" becomes "a wallet that reads the slot as plaintext entropy".
- Scenarios: sealed daemon answers 503 except health; unseal with the wrong passphrase refused, right one starts the scheduler; missing configured file fails startup.

Hand-off (done-condition 6): the reference stores plaintext entropy today; it implements the slot, the sealed state and the unseal route.

Owners: SEC-25, the new STO rule, HST-2/3/4/6/10/29, API-8/16/25/37, CNF-47. spec-ee9 and spec-11k depend on this bead.

## PR #15 review corrections to ADR-0033 (2026-10-01) — additive, ADR-0033 governs
- `POST /v1/unseal` is accepted only while the daemon is bound to loopback (SEC-3 gives the set no transport security); an operator binding beyond loopback uses the passphrase file, or reaches a loopback bind through an authenticated tunnel.
- The sealed start order: load config → log → re-assert the data directory → take the store LOCK and read the TOKEN file under it (HST-33; the token is a file, not in a store) → bind the listener → sealed (health answers with the flag, everything else 503) → on unseal: open both stores → seed or validate the policy row → load the seed → open clients → scheduler. HST-6 currently fuses "take the lock and open both stores"; split it.
- The standalone and one-shot flag names a passphrase FILE, never the passphrase (argv and shell history expose it); otherwise the configured file or a TTY prompt.
- A store written before ADR-0033 is retired by restoring its mnemonic into a new encrypted store (`restore-mnemonic`); no in-place conversion is specified.

## PR #15 round 2 correction (2026-10-01) — supersedes the "init creates the encrypted slot" sentence above
`init` writes NO seed (HST-4 creates the stores, policy row and token; SEC-11: the first serve mints; the order is `init → restore-mnemonic → serve`). The encrypted slot is first written by `restore-mnemonic` (passphrase from the configured file, a flag naming a file, or a TTY prompt) or by the first serve, which mints only from the configured passphrase file and otherwise refuses to start, minting nothing (SEC-11's existing "refuse when the key source is not available"). The unseal call never mints; it only decrypts an existing slot. HST-4 therefore does NOT gain a passphrase requirement; the first-serve path in HST-6 and SEC-11 does.

## PR #15 round 3 correction (2026-10-01) — supersedes "no store opened" while sealed
The sealed start opens both stores far enough to read whether the seed slot EXISTS (its presence and discriminator, never its contents) — the only way to choose the path: seeded + no passphrase file → bind and wait sealed; seedless + no passphrase file → refuse to start, minting nothing (SEC-11). While sealed: no federation client opened, no store written, no scheduler or watchdog, every route but health 503. HST-6's sealed branch says exactly this.

## PR #15 round 9 consistency corrections (2026-10-01) — additive; the ADR governs
- While sealed, `POST /v1/unseal` is SERVED (it is not one of the 503 routes); API-37 gains the sealed 503 message.
- A seeded store with no passphrase file bound beyond loopback fails startup (HST-29): nothing could unseal it.
- The first serve mints only on a store holding the standing-instruction acceptance record `init` writes (ADR-0035); SEC-11 gains that precondition.
- SEC-25's fail-closed sentence is restated: missing/unreadable/wrong configured file, no file on a seedless store, or no file on a seeded store bound beyond loopback → refuse to start; no file on a seeded loopback store → sealed. CNF-47 gains the sealed case beside its key-unavailable case.
- While sealed the policy row (STO-13) is validated read-only and seeded only after unseal.
- Owners of the passphrase input: HST-5 and HST-2 for `walletd mnemonic`/`restore-mnemonic` (flag naming a file, or a prompt); HST-10 and API-25 for the standalone flag only.

## Owner decisions after the four-reviewer rules review (2026-10-02) — supersede anything above that disagrees
The first serve mints from the configured passphrase file alone; it does NOT check the standing-instruction acceptance record (dropped: the daemon cannot serve a store `init` did not create, and ADR-0035 says nothing checks acceptance at runtime). SEC-11 gains no acceptance precondition.

title: OPS-45 pre-fund admission at the fourth killpoint can terminalize a committed send (Invoiced not exempt)
description:
Sections below were written in up to three review rounds; where they disagree, the latest section governs.
BLOCKER, R3, verified. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:259-264 (OPS-45): for Move and DirectInflow pre-fund admission runs BEFORE reassembly (OPS-20) and is skipped only when the cached record is trusted and its phase is Sending | Settled | Refunded | Failed | Stranded — Invoiced is not exempt. 03:100-103 (OPS-7): amount + fee_cap <= balance[from] - reservations.outbound(from), sampled fresh. 03:584 (OPS-28, fourth killpoint): send committed; the record lacks the send operation id — required resume is backfill, or a re-pay deduplicates to already in flight. 03:271-272: its refusal is Permanent and terminalizes the intent.
Scenario: a source holding just enough for amount + fee_cap; the send commits and debits it; the process dies before the send op id is written; on restart the record is Invoiced, OPS-45 runs the OPS-7 arithmetic on the debited balance, fails insufficient_after_reservations, and the intent is Failed while the outgoing contract is in flight. Contradicts OPS-28 exactly-once and CNF-12 (10:92).
Fix: for Move/DirectInflow run reassembly (discover committed artifacts by move_id / dedup) before pre-fund admission, or exempt Invoiced when the send is found committed; state which. Add a killpoint-4 scenario with a tightly funded source, once with the pre-receive draft cache present and once after cache loss.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-reviewer bead review: R1, R2, R3, R4)
CONFIRMED by all four; understated (R2): a second trigger is the DESTINATION check — at killpoint 4 the swap may already have completed, so balance[to] already includes amount and OPS-7's 'balance[to] + reservations.inbound(to) + amount <= per_fed_cap' counts it twice (over_cap even with a well-funded source). DirectInflow has the same exposure: a crash after the invoice write but before the Awaiting write re-performs an Executing intent with cached phase Invoiced; if the payer already paid, the destination is double-counted. Corrected fix (one formulation, R4; keyed on reassembled artifacts, not on the undefined 'trusted' — R1, R2): in OPS-45, for Move and DirectInflow run reassembly (OPS-20: cache, then the operation log by move_id / correlation key) BEFORE pre-fund admission; then skip the SOURCE arithmetic when the reassembled record has a send operation id (killpoints 2-3 still need it: the send is new funding), and skip the DESTINATION arithmetic when a receive artifact exists (invoice or receive operation id). Exempting every Invoiced record without the lookup is wrong (R3): it would admit an unfunded invoice without the fresh checks. Owner OPS-45; OPS-19, OPS-7 ('again at perform time') and CONTEXT.md Reassembly keep citing it; OPS-35's optional pre-step backfill becomes irrelevant. Scenario here (not in the coverage bead): amend CNF-12 or add CNF-55 — killpoint 4 with a tight source, with the destination at cap minus amount, with the pre-receive draft cache present and lost.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-reviewer bead review round 2: R1, R2, R3, R4)
CONFIRMED (P0). Fold in the unfiled minor that lives next door: OPS-19 'share one plan and one step loop' is a code-structure sentence that fails the refactor test — reword to the shared observable semantics while editing OPS-45's neighbour. CNF-55 is the next free CNF (verify). spec-tc0 no longer lists OPS-45; the killpoint-4 scenario is this bead's alone. spec-bsk lands after this (the rewrite removes one 'trusted' use).

## Third review (2026-09-23, round 3: R1, R2, R3, R4) — where sections disagree, THIS section governs
One correction to the corrected fix (R2): the destination skip is too broad for Move. At killpoints 2-3 (invoice minted, no send) balance[to] does not yet include the amount — the move's invoice is never surfaced, only the move's own send can pay it — so the destination check is not a double count there and skipping it weakens the per-federation cap. Rule: Move → skip BOTH checks only when the reassembled record has a send operation id (killpoint 4 or later), otherwise run both; DirectInflow → skip the destination check when a receive artifact exists (the payer may already have paid). Wording: at killpoint 4 the cache is the Invoiced record, not 'the pre-receive draft cache'.

title: FMI-17 send dedup (and FMI-30/38/39/41) describe the fork SDK, not upstream: make the guarantees wallet-enforced
description:
BLOCKER, R3 + R2, verified for FMI-17 against the local checkout. 02-fedimint-integration.md:235-237 (FMI-17): an lnv2 send is deduplicated by an operation id derived from the invoice: one payment attempt per invoice per client; a second send MUST NOT fund a second outgoing contract. 03:347 (raw pay) and 03:151-153 (OPS-10, retry refused with this invoice already consumed its single payment attempt) rest on it. The local fork (bradleystachurski/fedimint, modules/fedimint-lnv2-client/src/lib.rs:567-570) pins the attempt index to 0 with the comment that older clients derived a fresh index per payment attempt; upstream master derives OperationId from (invoice, attempt) and lets a failed/refunded attempt be followed by a new one. An implementer on the public SDK therefore funds a second contract after an unrecorded, later-refunded send — exactly what FMI-17 forbids — and never sees the dead operation the text promises.
R2 lists the other rules the withdrawn FMI-1 recorded as fork patches: FMI-30 (complete-or-fail within 600 s of no progress), FMI-38 (5-minute bounded re-issued waits), FMI-39 (single-share decryption), FMI-41 (claim retried until expiry). Each is a legitimate requirement but presupposes SDK behaviour the public SDK may not have.
Fix: (a) make the no-second-attempt guarantee a wallet rule: persist the operation id before issuing the send (already the raw path's order) and refuse a second send of any invoice that has a recorded operation id regardless of the terminal, including after a missing artifact write; state the disposition of terminal failed/refunded sends explicitly; (b) a chapter-02 note (or a row per rule) naming which FMI behaviours an upstream SDK may not provide, so an implementer knows to enforce them above the SDK; (c) a restart scenario: send issued, artifact write lost, send refunded, restart — no second contract.
close_reason: Premise false (R2, R3, R4; re-verified against /home/master/p/fedimint whose origin is upstream fedimint/fedimint): single-attempt lnv2 send dedup is upstream since v0.12.0 (commit 703a37e8f3f, 2026-07-10); the code repo's pin 72b1e5be has it too. FMI-17 and OPS-17 describe the public SDK. FMI-30/38/39/41 are already MUSTs on the wallet; whether an SDK release provides them is a code-repo finding, and a chapter-02 SDK-version note would fail the refactor test (ADR-0032). The fix's claim that the raw path persists the op id before the send was also wrong (OPS-17: issue, then persist; the hash lookup covers the crash window). Residual: FMI-17 says 'the protocol derives' where it is the client that derives (wording nit); the send-issued / artifact-lost / refunded / restart scenario moves to the coverage bead.

title: Gross-up: FMI-18 selects an over-crediting contract, FMI-15 says never more and misstates what the receive quote covers; OPS-44 cites a nonexistent fixed point
description:
Sections below were written in up to three review rounds; where they disagree, the latest section governs.
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-reviewer bead review; this text replaces the original and the merged spec-pcr text (both premises were partly wrong, see below).

**The contradiction (verified).** 02-fedimint-integration.md:213-219 (FMI-15): the destination is credited "never more, and possibly less by a bounded shortfall … the best verified under-crediting candidate". 02:267-268 (FMI-18): `gross_up(net, gateway_fee, fed_fee)` is "the smallest invoice amount such that `contract = invoice − gw(invoice)` and `contract − fed(contract) ≥ net`" — the `≥` selects the OVER-crediting side when the step function has no exact solution, the case FMI-15 expressly contemplates. 03:449-450 (OPS-44) cites "(`FMI-18`, `OPS-22`'s fixed point)"; OPS-22 (03:502-513) defines no fixed point — the phrase exists only in CONTEXT.md:128-129 (Delivered net). OPS-23 (03:536) checks only equality of quoted and committed contracts, so it cannot catch an over-crediting quote.

**A false protocol statement in the set (verified at the pin 72b1e5be and at upstream master).** FMI-15:218 says the federation's "mint output fee on the claim" is one "which the lnv2 receive quote does not include". That is wrong: `receive_fee_quote` (modules/fedimint-lnv2-client/src/lib.rs:827 at the pin) calls `Client::fee_quote`, which "runs the exact same primary-module balancing (`create_final_inputs_and_outputs` …)" and whose result covers the Lightning input fee, the mint change-output fees and sub-denomination dust; only the gateway's off-chain fee is excluded. So the merged spec-pcr premise ("delivered net omits the mint output fee") was false, and the round-1 formula `credited = invoice − receive_quote − mint_fee` would subtract the mint fee twice. Do not use it.

**The real residual (R2, verified).** The federation quote is "point-in-time: it depends on the current inventory" (client.rs:814); the mint lays out change against the wallet's note inventory at CLAIM time, and the per-note fee applies per change note. The quote is taken when the invoice is minted; the claim is priced when it lands. So the credited amount can differ from `invoice − receive_quote` in EITHER direction, and "never more" cannot be guaranteed at mint time unless the mint's per-note fee is zero.

**Fix, one owner each.**
- FMI-15 owns the vocabulary, defined once: requested net `N`; invoice `I`; gateway receive fee `G(I)`; incoming contract `C = I − G(I)`; federation receive quote `F(C)` = the whole claim transaction's fee as quoted at mint time (Lightning input fee + mint output fees + dust — say so, and delete the "does not include" clause); **delivered net** `= C − F(C)` as quoted (this is what `receive_quote` already means in OPS-18/OPS-44: "`actual = amount − committed + the federation's receive quote on committed`", "`delivered = invoice − receive_quote`"); **credited** = what the balance actually rose by. "Never more" binds the delivered net. State the credited-vs-delivered variance bound (the mint's per-note fee × the change-note-count difference) or state that the set does not bound it.
- FMI-18 owns the gross-up contract: the exact solution when one exists, else the candidate whose quoted delivered net is the largest not exceeding `N`, ties to the smallest invoice; the shortfall bound (one receive-fee step); the no-solution case; the 5 000 msat minimum-contract case by citation to FMI-16 (OPS-22 already maps it to `Permanent("direct inflow amount too small: …")` — keep and cite). Correct the inequality.
- OPS-44 drops "OPS-22's fixed point"; CONTEXT.md:128-131 aligns (it says "Every ENFORCED fee cap is computed from the delivered net", which contradicts OVR-7's funding-move planned-cap exception at 00:57-59 — OVR-7 owns, the glossary cites). OVR-7's "what the destination is actually credited" becomes "the delivered net (FMI-15)"; ALC-21's `invoice − receive_quote` IS the delivered net, no change of basis needed. executive-summary.md:62-63 and :73-75 restate the same rules — cite.
- Scenarios: the environment header (10:26-27 "'rises by the amount' … are exact"), CNF-9 (already "minus the gateway and federation receive fees"), CNF-11 (10:87-88), CNF-12 (10:95), CNF-13, CNF-42 (10:155 asserts "exactly once" — multiplicity, not amount; leave) assert exact credits with no fee fixture. Either fix the environment's mint per-note fee at zero and say so in the header (then delivered = credited and the exact assertions hold), or assert the delivered net at the ledger (STO-17 stamps it) and bound the balance change by CNF-10's rule. CNF-10's "at most 1 000 msat less" gets the same treatment.

Owners: FMI-15, FMI-18; cite from OVR-7, ALC-21, OPS-22/23/24/44, CNF-9/10/11/12/13. Hand-off (done-condition 6): none for the pin — the pin already quotes this way; the spec text was the error.

Depends on nothing. spec-bqv (route cost) and spec-tc0's exact-credit assertions depend on this vocabulary.

## Third review (2026-09-23, round 3: R1, R2, R3, R4) — where sections disagree, THIS section governs
Precision (R2, R3): (1) name receive_quote explicitly — in OPS-22/OPS-26/OPS-44 receive_quote ≡ G(I) + F(C) (OPS-26: 'receive_quote = invoice_msat − rec.amount'); state that identity in FMI-15 so F is not conflated with receive_quote. (2) More restatements carry 'actually credited' and must cite FMI-15 instead: ALC-21 (06:297-299 'what the destination is actually credited'), CONTEXT.md Delivered net (:126-127), API-21 ('the destination is credited amount, never more'), DOM-7's table, SEC-8. (3) The variance bound 'per-note fee × change-note-count difference' is NOT established: mint balancing can also consolidate existing notes (input fees) and dust can change; DECIDED: the set does not bound credited-vs-delivered (the claim-transaction fee is inventory-dependent in every component); 'never more' binds the DELIVERED net; scenarios assert the delivered net at the ledger (STO-17) and the environment fixes zero mint fees and a 1 msat smallest denomination so that credited == delivered there. (4) ALC-27:373 requires 'candidate.spendable == baseline + delivered_in (exact equality)' — under a quote-only delivered net an uncontaminated probe can fail that check when claim-time fees differ; resolve it (assert the credited amount from the ledger, or bound it) and note the destination-cap consequence of upward variance; spec-xm8 depends on this. (5) The zero-fee fixture must also fix dust: credited equals delivered only if the smallest denomination is 1 msat — say so in the environment header. (6) Drop the stale sentence 'spec-tc0's exact-credit assertions depend on this vocabulary'; the users are spec-bqv, spec-pz6 (CNF-14) and spec-xm8.

title: OPS-10 lets a Failed send-required move be retried after 'send failed:' / 'receive failed:' (double-send, also after cache loss); older attempts are unaddressable by API-42
description:
BLOCKER (P0). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the third four-reviewer bead review; this text replaces every earlier version. Where anything elsewhere disagrees with this text, this text governs. The claimability half lives in spec-u3u — do not duplicate it here.

**The defect (verified).** 03:151-163 (OPS-10): retry is refused only for "a `Failed` pay that recorded an operation id" and "a `Failed` move whose move record's phase is `Stranded`"; the retry write "deletes the cached move record, appends a fresh ledger row and repoints the key index". 02:313-326 (FMI-37) send row, case (b): after `send failed:` the outgoing contract "WAS funded and its position is unresolved" and the wallet "cannot tell" (a) from (b). 04:580-584 (API-42): `{key}` names "the operation whose contract reached a terminal non-claim" — after a retry the key resolves to the new attempt. So a `Move` whose send reached the SDK's terminal `Failure` (OPS-27 maps `Failed(msg) → Failed`) can be retried by the user, which mints a new invoice and sends AGAIN while attempt 0's outgoing contract may be funded and attempt 0's receive state machine still runs in the destination client. A double-send under OVR-2's exactly-once property.

**A second path to the same double-send — cache loss.** OPS-10's `Stranded` guard reads the CACHED move record's phase, and STO-11:233 says the terminal phase "survive[s] only in this row". After cache loss a `Stranded` move (send settled, receive terminal non-claim; its ledger error begins `receive failed:`) has no record, the guard passes, and the retry sends again. spec-dgj's reassembly runs at perform, after the retry write has already advanced the attempt, so it does not close this.

**Guard — decided, do not re-derive.** OPS-10 refuses, permanently, the retry of a `Failed` intent whose action is send-required (`Move`, `Evacuate`; STO-11 fixes `send_required = false` for a receive-only `DirectInflow`, which can never carry these prefixes) and whose LEDGER error begins `send failed:` or `receive failed:` — the two prefixes HST-32 fixes as the operator's anchors — whatever the cached record says. Refused `conflict` with a named message (e.g. "this move's send was issued; its outgoing contract's position is unresolved"), classified by OPS-39/API-6 as 409. The durable ledger row (STO-15, STO-35) is the evidence, so cache loss changes nothing. Why permanent: after `FinalSendOperationState ∈ Success | Refunded | Failure` the send state machine never runs again and no verb in the set reads an outgoing contract's position; a verifying preimage (FMI-23) proves PAYMENT and forbids a new send, it never releases the guard; only authoritative evidence of no funding or a completed refund could justify a new payment, and the set has no reader for it. A fresh key (a new occurrence or nonce) is always available. Note the existing `Stranded` guard becomes a special case of this one; keep HST-32's wording aligned. A `receive failed:` DirectInflow or raw Receive stays retryable (its retry rule is spec-s2p's), but its old funded contract must remain addressable (below).

**Older-attempt addressability.** OPS-10 keeps "two truthful rows", STO-15 keeps the operation ids in them, STO-20 keeps older rows addressable by `seq`, and the client operation log survives. What is missing is the WIRE contract for API-42 to address an older attempt. API-42 locates the receive operation by the attempt correlation keys in the operation log (STO-34: the key, then `retry:<len>:<key>:<n>`). Decide the shape in the edit: API-42 returns one `outcome`, so `reclaim {key}` MUST accept an explicit attempt selector (a query parameter naming the attempt, default newest) — an API that addresses only the newest attempt cannot recover the older contract this finding is about, so that option is out; if one call may process several contracts, define the response. The selector is a wire change to API-42 and CNF-26 and to the CLI verb (spec-ee9 depends on it). Applies to moves, direct inflows and raw receives alike.

**Owners.** OPS-10 (the refusal and the retry write), STO-34 (correlation keys), API-42 (addressing), HST-32 (evidence). Scenarios, stated on planted store states (a send `Failure` needs a funding transaction rejected at consensus, which an honest environment cannot produce): a `Failed` move row with `send failed:` → retry refused 409 with the message; the same with the cache deleted → still refused; a `receive failed:` direct inflow retried → the old attempt's contract addressable by `reclaim {key}?attempt=0`.

Depends on spec-u3u (what API-42 may claim). spec-5gn, spec-s2p, spec-ee9 and spec-72e depend on this one.

title: OPS-18 over-cap raw receive publishes its invoice before the Permanent outcome lands; OPS-16 / API-21 return it as payable
description:
Sections below were written in up to three review rounds; where they disagree, the latest section governs.
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-reviewer bead review; this text replaces the original (which cited OPS-22 — the rule is OPS-18) and its round-1 correction.

**The defect (verified).** 03-operation-lifecycle.md:385-388 (OPS-18, raw Receive committed-fee check): "`actual > fee_cap` → persist the operation id and invoice **first**, so the orphan is recorded, then `Permanent(…)`". 03:302-304 (OPS-16): the invoice target resolves "as soon as the intent's invoice or the move record's invoice exists". 04-api-contract.md:297-299 (API-21): 409 `failed` only for a terminal intent WITHOUT an invoice, and "Re-submitting the same key re-yields the same invoice (OPS-8)". OPS-13: a fenced write that applies "wakes every waiter parked on the key"; API-21 blocks "up to 30 seconds for the invoice artifact". So the artifact write wakes the waiters and the payer receives an invoice the wallet has already judged over cap, BEFORE the `Permanent` outcome lands, and again on every resubmission; meanwhile the terminalized intent releases its reservation (OPS-9 reserves only non-terminal intents) while the invoice stays payable for up to 3 600 s.

**Fix — pick ONE publication rule and state it; the two candidates:**
- (preferred, no new field, mirrors the move path) OPS-24 already says a refused receive "MUST NOT take the invoice, which is never surfaced". Apply the same to the raw receive: OPS-18 records the operation id (the orphan) and its `Failed` disposition in ONE transaction (STO-16 already puts the ledger row in the same transaction as any status change), and does NOT publish the invoice: OPS-16's invoice target resolves only for a non-`Failed` intent, and waiters woken by that write see a terminal without an invoice, so API-21's existing 409 rule is already right. Publication eligibility and artifact visibility are then atomic; "check status after an earlier artifact write" does NOT close the race (R3).
- (alternative) keep recording the invoice but make API-21 answer 409 for a `Failed` intent whatever artifacts it holds. NOT "any terminal intent": `Done` must keep re-yielding its invoice (API-21, OPS-8).

**Consequences to state, not ask.** (i) The orphan, if paid out of band, is claimed by the SDK's own receive state machine for that operation (`Pending → Claiming → Claimed`, verified at the pin and master); the wallet initiates nothing; the only accounting question is that the `Failed` row keeps its error while the balance rises — say the ledger keeps the failure evidence and FMI-41's re-claim covers a rejected claim. With the preferred rule this cannot happen unless the wallet leaked the invoice. (ii) Retry: OPS-10 refuses only a `Failed` PAY that recorded an operation id, so this `Failed` receive IS retryable, and it mints a second invoice while the orphan is live — decide whether OPS-10 refuses a `Failed` receive that recorded an operation id, symmetric with pay, or allows it with the older contract addressable by API-42 (spec-cuw's addressing). The separate defect that a retry RE-ADOPTS the old operation id has its own bead.

Owners: OPS-18, OPS-16, API-21; OPS-10 for the retry decision. Scenarios here: a waiter already attached when the over-cap outcome is recorded receives 409, not the invoice; re-submission of the failed key → 409; a retry with the older invoice still payable.

Depends on spec-cuw (the retry/addressing decision). The paid-orphan dependency on spec-u3u was dropped: the SDK claims on its own.

## Third review (2026-09-23, round 3: R1, R2, R3, R4) — where sections disagree, THIS section governs
Corrections: (1) the retry decision is spec-s2p's (one owner): the answer is ALLOWED — under the preferred rule the failed attempt's invoice was never surfaced, so a retry mints a fresh invoice harmlessly; delete consequence (ii)'s either/or and cite s2p. (2) Two more owners must change: 02:226 (FMI-16) 'The wallet MUST persist the (operation id, invoice) pair the moment the call returns' and 03:528 (OPS-24) 'operation id and invoice persisted first' need the narrow exception (the pair is persisted in the same transaction as the Failed disposition; the invoice is recorded as evidence but never published) or aligned wording. (3) 'Cannot happen unless the wallet leaked the invoice' is false: the gateway created the invoice and can pay or route it independently; say instead that the SDK's receive state machine ATTEMPTS the claim of a paid orphan (issuance is not guaranteed — spec-u3u's four states apply). (4) Re-submission of a Failed key goes through the retry path, not API-21's re-yield: OPS-8 says 'Failed → the retry path (OPS-10) for a User request', so API-21's 'Re-submitting the same key re-yields the same invoice' and API-41's nonce-less direct-inflow re-yield are true only for live and Done keys — correct both sentences; the scenario 'resubmission → 409' holds only while the fee stays over the cap. (5) Say whether Intent.invoice is written at all under the preferred rule (if not, the OPS-16 non-Failed clause is redundant). Edge: this bead lands before spec-s2p (s2p → 5gn).

title: Supersession marker: OPS-31 says the retired parent keeps it, CNF-24 asserts it is cleared
description:
Sections below were written in up to three review rounds; where they disagree, the latest section governs.
MAJOR, R3, verified. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:617-620 (OPS-31): the marker is cleared by ... the exchange (the retired parent keeps it). 10-conformance-checklist.md:145-147 (CNF-24): the parent is Failed as superseded with its marker cleared. 01-domain-model.md:181 requires preservation of the parent's evidence.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-reviewer bead review: R1, R2, R3, R4)

One addition (R3): fix OPS-31's projection too — it currently yields false for a readable intent WITHOUT a marker and leaves a terminal intent WITH retained evidence uncovered; align with API-33: true only for the live Pending evacuation carrying the marker, false for every other readable intent, omitted only when no intent is readable. CNF-24's assertion lands here, not in the coverage bead. DOM-20, STO-25 align.

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-reviewer bead review round 2: R1, R2, R3, R4)

The sentence to rewrite is OPS-31's own 'cleared by … the exchange (the retired parent keeps it)', which contradicts itself; OPS-31:626-628's three-case projection ('true for an exact readable Pending agent Evacuate with a marker, false for an exact readable intent without one, omitted when no intent is readable') has no case for a Failed parent WITH a retained marker — align to API-33:461 ('false = the intent is readable but not live'). The evidence survives in the STO-25 sidecar (refusal) whichever way the marker goes, so 'evidence preservation' does not force 'keep'; keeping is simply the reading that matches OPS-31's parenthetical and API-33. Align DOM-20/STO-25. The CNF-24 assertion is this bead's alone.

title: Send fee admission is not bound to the contract actually funded: the SDK re-reads routing_info inside send and the pin's limit check is lexicographic; OPS-29 must state the total-cost property
description:
BLOCKER (P0). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the third four-reviewer bead review; this text replaces every earlier version. Where anything elsewhere disagrees with this text, this text governs.

**SDK facts — verified at the pin 72b1e5be, v0.12.1 and origin/master.** `send(invoice, gateway, custom_meta)` (pin modules/fedimint-lnv2-client/src/lib.rs:574-606) re-reads `routing_info` inside the call, computes `send_parameters(&invoice)` from what it read then, and funds `send_fee.add_to(amount)` at those terms. The pin's limit check (`lib.rs:590` `send_fee.le(&PaymentFee::SEND_FEE_LIMIT)`) uses a DERIVED `PartialOrd`, i.e. lexicographic on `base` first: a gateway posting `base` = 99 sat passes with ANY `parts_per_million`, so at the pin the funded fee is NOT bounded by FMI-19's envelope (100 sat + 1.5 %) — it can approach the payment amount. That, not "the SDK needs a patch", is why P0 stands. The wallet CAN bind the terms on the pinned SDK with no patch: `LightningClientInit.gateway_conn: Option<Arc<dyn GatewayConnection>>` is public (`lib.rs:222`), `send()` and `receive()` read `routing_info` through it, so a wallet-supplied connection can return the admitted terms or fail when the gateway's current terms differ. `send_with_terms` (upstream 9120506f70d / 2eed40ae3ef, in no tag; refuses ANY change, cheaper included, with `TermsChanged`) is the other route on master. Do not write into the set that the property is unimplementable.

**The defect in the set (verified).** 03:557 (move send step) and 03:353 (raw pay) run the cap check on the QUOTE, then issue the send. 07:164 (SEC-7) distinguishes wallet caps from the protocol schedule limits. A gateway can quote within the wallet's cap and then raise its fee before the send reads it; the funded contract exceeds what was admitted, and nothing in the set forbids it.

**Fix — one property, one owner, decided.**
- Owner OPS-29 (where caps bind and on what base; SEC-7 cites it). Property (A): the TOTAL funded cost of the send leg — the fee the funded outgoing contract carries plus the federation's send quote on it — together with the leg the cap already covers on the receive side, MUST fit the admitted cap, or nothing is funded. For a move the cap covers both legs: 03:558 (OPS-26) "the fixed receive quote alone over the cap → `Permanent`, the total over → `Retryable`" — so the send-leg check is against the cap MINUS the fixed receive cost, never against the whole cap (that would spend the receive leg's allowance twice). Say whether the expiration delta (a lock-time term, not a fee) is bound. An implementation that refuses ANY change of terms (policy B, upstream's `send_with_terms`) satisfies (A) — say "need not fail on a cheaper re-quote", not "does not fail". Class: `Retryable` with a re-quote, consistent with OPS-26's total-over-cap `Retryable`; raw Pay's and the move send-leg's existing terminal semantics preserved. OPS-17 (pay) and OPS-26 (move send) cite; FMI-17's refusal table gains a "terms changed → `Retryable`, nothing funded" row by citation.
- ADR-0030:62-65: its residual ("the cap bounds what the wallet knowingly agrees to, not what such a gateway does afterwards") contradicts a universal funded-cost guarantee, break-glass sends included. Decide and write ONE dated amendment: the guarantee holds for every send, break-glass included (recommended — the break-glass gateway is still a gateway the wallet quotes), and strike "Vetting is what normally covers that" (vetting binds nothing about fees). spec-y0b lands after this so ADR-0030 is amended once.

**Scenario here (not in the coverage bead):** a gateway raises its fee between the quote and the send by an amount that crosses the remaining allowance (an increase within the allowance is admitted under (A) — state both); the wallet funds nothing; the intent is `Retryable`, and the next attempt re-quotes. Chapter 10 forbids marking a scenario with a result (10:5-7).

**Hand-off (done-condition 6):** the reference implementation does not bind the terms today (an `Fn`); it can through the SDK's gateway-connection hook at the pin, or through `send_with_terms` after repointing. Record in the code repository's open findings; the same hook is the implementation point for FMI-40 on every gateway call (spec-22p).

## ADR-0030 already amended (2026-09-26) — do not amend it again
The residual in ADR-0030 ("the cap bounds what the wallet knowingly agrees to, not what such a gateway does afterwards. Vetting is what normally covers that") was withdrawn by a dated amendment at the top of ADR-0030: the funded-cost guarantee binds every send, the break-glass included. This bead's ADR item is done; write only the OPS-29 property and its citations. spec-y0b no longer needs to wait on this bead for ADR-0030.

title: Delivered net omits the mint output fee FMI-15 admits; CNF-11 demands an exact credit with no fee fixture
description:
MAJOR, R3, PLAUSIBLE. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:297 defines delivered net as invoice - receive_quote, what the destination is actually credited; 03:454 (OPS-44) sizes and enforces the cap on that arithmetic. 02-fedimint-integration.md:218 (FMI-15) admits the federation's mint output fee on the claim, which the lnv2 receive quote does not include. So the computed delivered net can exceed the real credit. 10-conformance-checklist.md:79 (CNF-10) tolerates a bounded shortfall while 10:87 (CNF-11) requires B to rise by exactly the amount, under an environment (10:20-27) that fixes no fee schedule.
Fix: define requested, quoted and credited amounts once and use the right one in each rule (cap enforcement on the quoted delivered net is fine if stated; balance assertions on the credited amount); rewrite CNF-11's assertion as a bound, or fix the fixture's fees so exactly is true, and say so.
close_reason: Merged into spec-1nc (one fee/credit arithmetic change, one owner) on all four reviewers' recommendation.

title: Storage result vs drive disposition: the chapter-05 intro and OPS-10/OPS-13 say every stale-attempt write is Retryable while STO-9's reset guard is Permanent — write the distinction, cite STO-9 not STO-8
description:
PRIORITY P2 (minor). Sections below were written in three rounds; where they disagree, the latest section governs.
MAJOR, R1, verified by quote. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:162-164 (OPS-10): every durable writer is attempt-fenced: a write by a stale attempt writes nothing, and a drive treats that as Retryable; 03:199-201 (OPS-13) the same for every artifact write. 05-persistence.md:186-190 (STO-9): the admission insert, a plain status write and the retryable reset report a differing stored attempt as a Permanent error; 03:256-257 (OPS-43): the reset requires the current Executing attempt, else Permanent. 03:54-58 (OPS-4): a journal failure MUST NOT produce a Failed intent. The class an implementer records, and the ledger error string (STO-35), differ by which rule is followed.
Fix: STO-9 owns it — a fenced write writes nothing and reports not-applied; a drive treats not-applied as Retryable and terminalizes nothing — and OPS-10, OPS-13, OPS-43 cite it.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-reviewer bead review: R1, R2, R3, R4)
DOWNGRADED to minor (R2: reconcilable as written; R1, R3: no behavioural divergence; R4: real but the OPS-4 appeal is misattributed). STO-9 already splits fenced writes into two groups (05:186-190): the admission insert, plain status write and retryable reset 'report a differing stored attempt as a Permanent error' (a STORAGE error class, STO-7), and 'every other fenced write … writes nothing and reports that it did not apply', which is what OPS-10/OPS-13's Retryable refers to. OPS-4 rules the first group ('terminalizes nothing … MUST NOT produce a Failed intent'). Nothing reaches the ledger error. Residual: 'Permanent' names both a storage error class and a perform outcome, and OPS-43's 'else Permanent' reads as the latter. Fix: a wording change in STO-9 — 'a stale-attempt refusal, never a perform outcome' — and OPS-43 cites it. Do NOT re-class the reset (STO-8 relies on 'Permanent on a failed guard').

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-reviewer bead review round 2: R1, R2, R3, R4)
CONFIRMED, P2. The permanent failed-attempt guard is in STO-9, not STO-8 (fix the citation). The chapter-05 introduction says 'Retryable and Permanent are the outcome classes of 03', so the storage-result vs drive-disposition distinction must be WRITTEN there, not assumed: a stale writer produces no mutation, and the caller's resulting disposition is unambiguous (STO-9, OPS-10/13/43).

## Third review (2026-09-23, round 3: R1, R2, R3, R4) — where sections disagree, THIS section governs
Correction (R4): the ORIGINAL contradiction claim is withdrawn — STO-9 already distinguishes 'the admission insert, a plain status write and the retryable reset report a differing stored attempt as a Permanent error' from 'every other fenced write … writes nothing and reports that it did not apply'. What remains is the round-2 residual only: write the storage-result vs drive-disposition distinction into the chapter-05 introduction and OPS-10/OPS-13's 'every stale write is Retryable' sentences (the reset's Permanent guard is the exception), fix the STO-8 → STO-9 citation, and do NOT reclassify the reset.

title: FMI-40 private-network gateway allowance has no home: add a walletd.toml key / standalone flag, default off
description:
MAJOR, R1 + R2, verified. 02-fedimint-integration.md:138-152 (FMI-40): MUST treat as unavailable — without connecting — a loopback, RFC 1918 or unique-local host; a host MAY offer an explicit configuration that permits private-network gateways — a test environment's gateways are on loopback — and that configuration MUST default to off. 08-hosts-and-deployment.md:19-24 (HST-2) and 08:40-50 (HST-3, five keys, MUST reject any other) leave no place for it. 10:20-27 puts every conformance gateway on a vetted list; 07:218-219 (SEC-18) says the build a scenario runs on is the implementation's own. On a release build every local harness gateway is unavailable and no money scenario can pass.
Fix: a sixth HST-3 key (and the standalone flag in HST-10), default off, named in FMI-40; or state in chapter 10's environment that gateways are reachable at public addresses.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-reviewer bead review: R1, R2, R3, R4)
DOWNGRADED to minor and RECAST (R3, R4: FMI-40 says a host 'MAY offer' the configuration, and chapter 10 does not require loopback gateways, so no contradiction exists and 'no money scenario can pass' was an unstated harness assumption; R1, R2 kept major on the practical ground that every local harness is loopback). Recast: an optional feature decision. If the product offers private-network gateways, the switch needs a home — a named HST-3 key (e.g. allow_private_gateways, default off), the standalone flag in the CLI grammar (spec-ee9), FMI-40 naming the owner and keeping 'MUST NOT affect the link-local and metadata rule'; its scope must match whatever spec-22p decides (gateways only, or every egress class). Fold the decision into spec-22p's list; nothing else to do here until it is taken.
close_reason: Merged into spec-22p (R1, R2, R3: an open bead with 'nothing to do until the decision is taken' misleads the ready queue). Residual carried by spec-22p: FMI-40's 'A host MAY offer an explicit configuration that permits private-network gateways' is a MAY no compliant host can exercise, because HST-2 owns the complete environment surface and HST-3 has five keys and MUST reject any other; spec-22p either files the chapter-11 entry for that allowance or strikes the MAY.

title: Discovery sources are unconfigurable and Nostr is never collected: implement ADR-0036 (Observer and NIP-87 Nostr by default, host configuration)
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-10-01: the product decision is taken (`ADR-0036`, docs/adr/0036-discovery-reads-the-observer-and-nostr-by-default.md). This text replaces every earlier version; read the ADR first.

**The gap (verified).** 02:433-434 (FMI-28) fetches `GET {base}/federations` but nothing says where `{base}` comes from; 06:396 (ALC-28 step 1) collects from `Observer, Manual` and never Nostr; 05:298 (STO-15) persists `DiscoverySource ∈ {Observer, Nostr, Manual}`; DOM-12 and FMI-43 say "No requirement in this set produces a Nostr candidate"; HST-3 is closed and the Policy row has no source field; CNF-17 and CNF-20 nonetheless need a discovery source. The reference's resident scheduler hard-codes `https://observer.fedimint.org/api`, so walletd has no operator knob.

**What ADR-0036 decided (do not re-open).** Both feeds on by default, both untrusted priors (ADR-0019, ADR-0020): nominate only; preview, structural check and probe gate before any funds move; never a trust, scoring or shutdown input. The Observer base is host configuration (a `walletd.toml` key and standalone flag), default `https://observer.fedimint.org/api`, empty disables it. Nostr reads NIP-87 kind-38173 announcements (`d` = federation id, `u` = one or more invite codes, `n` = network) from a relay list that is host configuration, default `wss://relay.damus.io`, `wss://nos.lol`, `wss://relay.primal.net`, `wss://relay.nostr.band`; empty disables Nostr. Kind-38000 recommendations are not read. A Nostr candidate gets FMI-28's identity check (claimed id, the invite's embedded id and the previewed config's computed id agree) and one more: an invite whose guardian endpoints are not the previewed config's endpoints is dropped (fedimint-observer#126 is the attack); a wrong network `n` is dropped before preview. DOM-12's and FMI-43's "no requirement produces Nostr" sentences go.
- ALC-28 step 1: collect from Observer, Nostr and Manual, in that order. Decide and state: the `<label>` values of `discover:<label>[:<index>]:<nonce>` keys (STO-6) for each source, and the Manual source's input (the invites the operator supplies through the CLI `discover --invite`, or a key).

- Chapter 10's environment names its discovery sources (a local Observer double and, or, a relay double); scenarios: a Nostr announcement with mismatched endpoints is dropped; an empty relay list disables Nostr.

Hand-off (done-condition 6): the reference collects no Nostr announcements and has no Observer knob on walletd.

title: Standing-instruction acceptance gates wallet creation and mnemonic restore (ADR-0035, ADR-0039), and no requirement records it yet
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-10-01: the decisions are taken (`ADR-0035`, the acknowledgement gates creation; `ADR-0039`, every wallet is auto-managed). This text replaces every earlier version — including the round-3 runtime inbound gate, which ADR-0035 rejected. Read both ADRs first.

**The gap (verified).** ADR-0014 requires "an explicit, plain-language, gating acknowledgement BEFORE any funds are received ('auto-managed across federations, best-effort, no guarantees, federations can fail, loss is possible, spending amounts only')". No requirement records it or gates on it: the API table (04:100), the admission checks (OPS-6) and the journal tag table (05:77) have no trace of it. The seeded policy row is not it: `init` writes that without the user.

**What is decided (do not re-open).**
- The acknowledgement gates CREATION and RESTORATION, not operations. `walletd init`, the standalone mode's first run and `restore-mnemonic` require explicit acceptance — a flag naming it, or a TTY prompt that shows the ADR-0014 text — and refuse to create or restore a store without it, leaving nothing behind (HST-29). The store records the acceptance (that it was given, which text, when) in its creation write. A store that exists was acknowledged: no runtime consent state, no acceptance route, no operation refused for lacking one.
- A backup that carries the acceptance record restores without asking (Android's Block Store, ADR-0003); a restore from a twelve-word mnemonic carries none and still asks.
- Every wallet is auto-managed (ADR-0039): no manual-only wallet, no automation-off state; the Policy bounds what the agent does. Chapter 11's question 1 is answered by ADR-0039.

**Edits.**
- A new domain rule, `DOM-22` (the next free DOM id; ADR-0035 cannot cite it until the rule exists, because the id gate refuses a citation of an undefined id — this bead is where the id is recorded): the acknowledgement's content (ADR-0014's phrases), that creation and restoration require it, that the store records it, that a backup able to carry it does, and that a store's existence is the proof. OVR-8 cites it as the onboarding presentation of the standing instruction.
- HST-4 (`init`), HST-10 and API-25 (the standalone flag), the `restore-mnemonic` contract, FMI-31 and SEC-11 cite it; HST-29 gains the refusal.
- The record's storage: part of the store's creation write — name the row (a journal row written once at creation, or the policy row's creation transaction gaining the record; it is never rewritten, so a WatchState field is unsuitable: STO-23 reseeds an absent WatchState). Count edits in STO-5/STO-29/STO-30 follow whichever is chosen.
- The backup unit gains the acceptance record wherever the backup can carry it: ADR-0025's backup unit, SEC-24 and FMI-32 (the headless operator's backup is the mnemonic, which carries none).
- Chapter 10's environment: its stores were created with the acceptance. Scenarios: `init` without acceptance creates nothing and exits non-zero; `restore-mnemonic` without acceptance likewise; with acceptance, the record is readable in the store.

Owners: the new DOM rule; OVR-8, HST-4/10/29, API-25, FMI-31, FMI-32, SEC-11, SEC-24 cite. Depends on nothing. spec-ee9 (the flag) and spec-11k (Android's creation and restore screens) depend on this bead.

## PR #15 round 9 consistency corrections (2026-10-01) — additive; the ADR governs
- Only ADR-0003's Block Store payload carries the acceptance record. The twelve-word mnemonic plus invite codes (ADR-0025, SEC-24) carries none, so `restore-mnemonic` asks; SEC-24 and ADR-0025 say so. FMI-32 is not involved.
- SEC-11's first-serve mint requires the store's acceptance record (written by `init`), which closes the path where a seedless store from an older `init` would run without one.

## Owner decisions after the four-reviewer rules review (2026-10-02) — supersede anything above that disagrees
- Nothing checks the acceptance record at runtime, the first serve's mint included; SEC-11 gains no precondition.
- `walletd restore-mnemonic` restores into a store `init` created, which already holds the record, so it does NOT ask again; the acceptance is asked where a store is created (`init`, the standalone first run, the Android app's creation and restore screens). The CLI grammar's acceptance flag is on `init` and the standalone first run only.
- A backup carries the record only where its format can (today Block Store); the mnemonic plus invites carries none.

title: Android host contract is missing from chapter 08: write HST-34 onward applying ADR-0003, 0011, 0031, 0035 and 0039
description:
MAJOR (P1; promoted 2026-10-01). Rewritten 2026-10-01: the Android host is in this version's scope, and its contract is written now. This text replaces every earlier version (which proposed a scope sentence excluding Android).

**The gap (verified).** 00:23-26 (OVR-1) makes chapter 08 the owner of every host's contract; chapter 08 specifies `walletd`, the standalone mode, the CLI and the browser sidecar only. - Watchdog and restart: the Android equivalent of HST-7/ALC-40's exit-and-restart (a stalled engine is torn down and restarted in-process at the next wake; nothing is lost).

title: Evacuation hop routing is owned by the glossary and ADR-0029 only; no FMI/OPS rule, no deadline, no hop scenario
description:
Sections below were written in up to three review rounds; where they disagree, the latest section governs.
MAJOR, 4/4 reviewers, verified. CONTEXT.md:223-241 (Shared route / Hop) states the loop normatively: ranked together, cheapest composed cost among different-node combinations first, the next tried when the first sizes to nothing viable, a failed hop sets aside that node pair. docs/adr/0029:50-84 gives the composed-cost formula, tie-break (lower receive fee, then the ordered pair of URLs) and per-attempt deadline — by function name (quote_fresh_send_required_cost, FreshMoveCost::total_fee), which fails the refactor test. 00-overview.md:104-108 (OVR-13) and 02:197-201 (FMI-14) say in ADR-0029's order; 03:435-440 (OPS-21) snapshots one gateway fee per leg without saying how the two gateways are chosen; 02:282-297 (FMI-22) bounds the fallback scan at 10 s and names no bound for the class scan. Chapter 10 cites OVR-13 zero times: the environment (10:20-27) always has a shared gateway G, CNF-14 uses it, CNF-53 is one break-glass gateway — a shared-route-only implementation passes.
Fix: FMI-44 (or extend FMI-14): candidate set = validated destination list x validated source list on distinct lightning_public_key; order by composed cost at the ask (ALC-13's formula), ties by lower receive fee then URL pair; next combination on an empty sizing result; one per-attempt deadline named in FMI-22; what journaled as truncated writes. CONTEXT.md and ADR-0029 cite it. Add a CNF with disjoint vetted lists on distinct Lightning nodes asserting route identities, both fee legs, committed-route replay and fallback after a failed performer.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-reviewer bead review: R1, R2, R3, R4)
CONFIRMED by all four; the fix needs more decisions named. (1) The proposed cost formula was WRONG (R3): ADR-0029:54 requires the FULL route cost including the federation quotes on the contracts gross-up implies (FMI-18/OPS-44), not ALC-13's planning model — rank by the actual composed cost, then the accepted tie-breaks. (2) The shared class's own candidate loop for an EVACUATION (amount sized, not final; 'try a candidate, size it, on nothing viable try the next, then the next class') — FMI-14's steps are written for a final amount. (3) The per-attempt deadline must be a named constant in FMI-22, because 'inside perform_timeout' is undefined when the timeout is 0 (R2); its relation to the perform budget; what a truncated search writes to the ledger row (a warning, an error text, nothing). (4) Which route's samples become the OPS-31 marker when both classes refuse (decides ALC-23 qualification). (5) A hop hint cannot be carried: Evacuate has one gateway? field (DOM-7) while the glossary says a hop hint is two identities — say so. (6) Cache-loss replay for hops: in STO-33 gateway names the gateway for THAT leg, so OPS-20 must reconstruct destination and source roles explicitly, never an undifferentiated newest gateway. (7) Set-aside (FMI-42) and the prohibition on switching after commitment. (8) The attempt-level sense of 'serves' ('serves this attempt') lives here (spec-hrb). Correct executive-summary.md:64-65, which says an ordinary move hops. FMI-44 only if no earlier FMI lands first. The hop CNF lands HERE: disjoint vetted lists on distinct Lightning nodes, cache loss both before and after the send record exists, route identities, both fee legs, fallback after a failed performer. Depends on spec-1nc (the composed cost uses the settled amount contract).

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-reviewer bead review round 2: R1, R2, R3, R4)
CONFIRMED; large (the one bead a fresh agent needs a plan for). Additions: (1) executive-summary.md:34-35 ('through one gateway that serves both federations or two when none does') also says an ordinary move hops, beside 64-65 — fix both. (2) ADR-0029:75-79's 'ONE per-attempt deadline … far enough inside perform_timeout' becomes an FMI-22 row. (3) Specify the FAILURE TRANSITIONS, not only pricing and order (R3): which failures abandon only the current candidate, advance from shared routing to a hop, end the attempt Retryable, supply structural refusal evidence, or set an endpoint/route aside; and that the shared-route search cannot consume the whole budget before the required hop fallback. (4) DOM-7's Evacuate {…, gateway?, …} is one field while CONTEXT.md:200-201 says a hint 'names a whole route … two gateway identities for a hop'; ALC-17 only ever stamps the pair's resolved_gateway, so a hop hint is never produced — delete the glossary sentence. FMI-44 is the next free FMI (highest defined 43; verify). Land after spec-shy (FMI-14 step 2's hint fallback is reused by the class loop) and spec-1nc (the composed cost is defined through FMI-18's gross-up); spec-hrb ('serves this attempt') and spec-y0b's hop note land after this. The OPS-20 hop-replay item is independent and may be split off.

## Third review (2026-09-23, round 3: R1, R2, R3, R4) — where sections disagree, THIS section governs
Split allowed (R2): (a) FMI-44 — candidate set, composed-cost order, tie-break, failure transitions, marker samples — with the FMI-22 deadline row and the hop CNF; (b) OPS-20 hop cache-loss replay (which operation's gateway is the destination leg); (c) the executive-summary and CONTEXT clean-ups. spec-7lk is a prerequisite (R4, R2): the hop route's set-aside uses FMI-42's selection-based exclusion contract, and this bead names set-aside behaviour in its failure transitions.

title: FMI-19 component-wise fee limit has no wallet-side enforcer; OPS-21 and ADR-0029 say the protocol refuses lexicographically
