title: Probe leg fee cap default is stated two incompatible ways (FMI-34 10 sats vs STO-13 max_fee 200 sats); STO-26's 'default-qualifying' is a misnamed fixed retention category
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the third four-reviewer bead review; this text replaces every earlier version. Where anything elsewhere disagrees with this text, this text governs.

**The defect (verified).** 02:461-462 (FMI-34): leg fee cap `max_fee` "(default 10 sats per leg in the standalone verb)". 05:257 (STO-13): seeded `max_fee 200_000` msat. 06:47-52 (ALC-3): "every planning and probing path MUST run under the stored Policy … its probe amount and leg fee cap (max_fee)". Two incompatible defaults for the same verb; both are live in the reference implementation (wallet-cli's `probe`: "PER-LEG fee cap in millisatoshis (default 10000 = 10 sats)"; every daemon money verb: `policy.max_fee`).

**Not defects.** 05:470-471 (STO-26) "default-qualifying means `ok && amount_msat ≥ 20_000 && leg_fee_cap_msat ≤ 10_000`" is a RETENTION category with two fixed constants, misnamed, not a third default; its `10_000` is the old CLI probe default (the reference hard-codes it in `ProbePolicy::default()`), NOT STO-13's seeded `max_fee` (200_000). Its effect is limited to which attempts survive beyond seven days (STO-26 first keeps every attempt within 7 days plus the newest and newest-ok per source). ALC-27's leg-OUT `min(leg_cap, delivered_in − out_net)` (06:371-374) is not a contradiction: a stricter OUT cap satisfies a per-leg maximum.

**Fix — decided.** FMI-34: delete "default 10 sats per leg in the standalone verb" and cite STO-13 (ALC-3 already makes the standalone probe run under the stored `max_fee`). STO-26: KEEP the predicate and its two constants (`20_000`, `10_000`) exactly, and RENAME the category so it no longer says "default" (e.g. "small-probe-qualifying"), stating that it is fixed and independent of any Policy value. Do NOT substitute STO-13's seeded values and do NOT key it to any policy — either is a retention redesign, a separate decision for chapter 11 if anyone wants it. One sentence of consequence: under the seeded policy (cap 200_000) no probe leg is ever in the category; that is harmless (the newest `ok` attempt per source is still kept) and the sentence belongs in STO-26. title: Both joins must write their candidate row with the registry row, and ALC-28 step 2's repair must key on FederationInfo.auto_joined (ADR-0038)
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-10-01: ADR-0038 supplies the provenance this bead found missing, and the set is greenfield (no store predates these rules). This text replaces every earlier version.

**The gap (verified).** 06:399-402 (ALC-28 step 2): a joined federation whose row is `Discovered`/`Rejected` "and whose registry entry is agent-created" becomes `AutoJoined`/`Passed`; a joined federation with no row gets one "(source: Manual, AutoJoined, Passed)". 05:83 (STO-5): `FederationInfo {invite, db_prefix, joined_at}` carried no actor, so "agent-created" was underivable and a hand-joined federation without a candidate row became probe-gated, against SEC-16 (07:198-202). 03:605-609 (OPS-42): a user join "marks" the candidate `UserApproved` only "from a state that is neither `AutoJoined` nor already `UserApproved`"; it does not say the row is created when none exists. DOM-3/ALC-37 probe-gate any joined federation without a `UserApproved` row, so if the row is not created the conformance environment's own A and B are probe-gated and CNF-13 refuses `NotProbed`.

**Decided (do not re-open).**
- ADR-0038: the registry row carries `auto_joined` (spec-60q adds it), written once with the membership. It is the "agent-created" fact.
- Greenfield: no legacy store holds user-joined federations without candidate rows; no migration or backfill is specified.

**Fix.**
1. Both joins write their candidate row in the SAME journal transaction as the registry row (FMI-8, "writes the registry row, and only then makes the client live", is shared by both and is an owner): a user `join` (OPS-42) writes `{source: Manual, structural: Passed, state: UserApproved}` when no row exists or the row is `Discovered`/`Rejected` — and leaves an existing `AutoJoined` row agent-owned and probe-gated, exactly as OPS-42:606 and SEC-16:200 say (only the audited `approve`, API-23, releases it); an auto-join writes `AutoJoined` with the registry row (otherwise a racing user join could find the registry row, see `Discovered`, and promote the agent's federation past SEC-16's gate). FMI-31's recovery already writes registry and `UserApproved` in one transaction — the precedent. DOM-12:100-101 gains "or from no row".
2. ALC-28 step 2 becomes a repair table keyed on `auto_joined`: a joined federation with no candidate row → create `{Manual, Passed, AutoJoined}` when `auto_joined` is true, `{Manual, Passed, UserApproved}` when false; a `Discovered` row with `auto_joined` true → `AutoJoined`; a row whose `structural` is `Rejected(reason)` → leave `structural` as it is and set only `state` per the same rule (no structural re-check inside the repair; the next discovery pass re-checks). Never demote `UserApproved` (STO-26). Distinguish an absent row from an unreadable one (an unreadable row is ALC-37's fail-closed case). With the atomic writes of item 1, this table only meets crash-free stores, so it is a consistency check, not a migration.
3. Do not infer provenance from the `join:<fed>:<nonce>` ledger row (best-effort under OVR-4).

**Scenario:** after a crash at any point of a user join, either there is no registry row or there is a registry row with a `UserApproved` row; a user `join` of a federation the agent already auto-joined leaves it `AutoJoined` until `approve`.

Owners: FMI-8, OPS-42, ALC-28, DOM-12. Depends on spec-60q (the `auto_joined` field). FederationInfo's field types are spec-tj5's.

title: OPS-11 / ALC-53 use 'world generation', 'plan authority', 'balance authority' and 'balance facts', none defined: replace with the owned counters and state the in-batch rule
description:
Sections below were written in up to three review rounds; where they disagree, the latest section governs.
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-reviewer bead review; this text replaces the original (which proposed DEFINING the three terms — do not) and its round-1 correction.

**The defect (verified).** 03-operation-lifecycle.md:167-169 (OPS-11): the batch MUST be refused whole on "a stale policy generation (ALC-41), a changed world generation, an invalid plan or balance-facts authority, or more than one occurrence". 06-allocator-and-automation.md:773-775 (ALC-53): "the world generation, the plan authority, the balance authority". CONTEXT.md:325-330 (Generation) defines exactly three counters — a balance generation per federation (OPS-13), a membership generation (OPS-6), a policy generation (ALC-41). Nothing defines issuance, content, invalidation or equivalence of "world generation", "plan authority", "balance authority" or "balance facts", so whole-batch acceptance cannot be implemented or reviewed independently.

**Fix — replace, don't define; no lease/token machinery (fails the refactor test).** OPS-11 enumerates the observable comparisons whose change rejects the batch whole, by CITATION to the owners (OPS-13's third bullet already states the balance-generation rule; OPS-6 already says every admission advances the membership generation "so that no allocator plan computed over the world before this admission can commit"; ALC-35: a plan is "valid only with the balance generation that authorized it"; ALC-41 the policy generation; OPS-41's fence: no plan or balance facts issued during a raw terminal write or membership change). Then state, in OPS-11, the two things implementations will otherwise do differently:
1. **What a "balance fact" is** — the sampled spendable balance per federation that the plan was computed over (FMI-27) — and that ALC-53 item 2 compares it by the federation's balance generation, not by value.
2. **Self-advance within a batch.** OPS-6 advances the balance generation of every federation the action touches and the membership generation on EVERY successful admission, including each decision the batch itself admits; unless the batch is exempt from its own advances, the second decision of any batch fails ALC-53 item 2. State the rule (recommended: the batch's comparisons are evaluated once, before its first admission, under one fence; the batch's own admissions do not invalidate its remaining decisions; any OTHER admission or a registry write in between rejects the rest of the batch whole).
Also: FMI-8 "A join MUST invalidate any allocator plan computed over the world before it (ALC-32)" — ALC-32 defines no invalidation, and OPS-6's membership generation is advanced by admission, not by the registry write that actually changes membership; make the join/open/recovery commit advance the membership generation (owner OPS-6 or OPS-42) so the race is closed.

ALC-53, ALC-34 (06:530-531), ALC-38 step 9 and the glossary cite OPS-11; ALC-38 step 5's "authorize planning" is the OPS-41 fence, not one of these. Decide OPS-39's `conflict — an admission racing a membership change (OPS-41)` row (a fresh-admission guard or plan invalidation only) and make owner and mapping agree; spec-euo edits the neighbouring OPS-39/API-15 rows, so land this first.

**Scenario:** a batch of two decisions; (a) a join commits between plan and commit → the whole batch is refused; (b) a user pay is admitted between the batch's first and second decision → state which of "whole batch refused" and "one decision dropped" applies, per the rule chosen in 2.

Owners: OPS-11; OPS-6 for the join advance. Depends on nothing.

## Third review (2026-09-23, round 3: R1, R2, R3, R4) — where sections disagree, THIS section governs
Corrections (R2, R3): (1) the batch commit is ONE serialized unit at the admission point (ALC-32: commit 'admits the planned batch through the admission point … and performs no network IO'); competing admissions and registry changes are ordered before or after it, never between two of its decisions. Then the in-batch rule reduces to 'the batch's own admissions never invalidate its remaining decisions', and scenario (b) becomes: a pay admitted between PLANNING and commit → the decisions touching its federation are dropped (item 2), the rest commit; a join committed between planning and commit → the whole batch refused. Every 'refused whole' sentence stays true. (2) The join-advance owner is OPS-41, not 'OPS-6 or OPS-42': its first sentence already enumerates 'a join, an open, a recovery commit', and auto-join builds no intent (DOM-7), so OPS-42 alone cannot own it. (3) Say WHY comparison is by generation, not value: the admission arithmetic (ALC-53 item 7, OPS-7) already re-checks fresh values, and a value comparison would drop decisions whenever the SDK balance moves with no journal write (a claimed receive). Also keep the original obligation to enumerate EVERY invalidating event, not only the named counters.

title: Journal key: STO-1 prefixes every key with 0x00, STO-5 says [tag] ++ id_bytes, STO-18 requires an exactly nine-byte ledger tail
description:
Sections below were written in up to three review rounds; where they disagree, the latest section governs.
MAJOR, R4, verified. 05-persistence.md:16-18 (STO-1): inside journal.db every journal key is prefixed 0x00, and a key outside that prefix is not part of the journal. 05:55 (STO-5): every journal key is [tag] ++ id_bytes, the ledger key 0x05 ++ be64(seq). 05:388-395 (STO-18): the tail is the lexicographically greatest 0x05 key, which MUST be a canonical nine-byte key; a tail key that is not exactly nine bytes is the fence. Two implementations write mutually unreadable stores.
Fix: state the raw byte sequence once in STO-5 (e.g. 0x00 ++ tag ++ id_bytes, with lengths), distinguish namespace prefix from logical key wherever a length or lexicographic rule appears (STO-18, STO-10 index keys), and correct the nine-byte sentences.

Fix, one sentence in STO-5: keys and lengths in this chapter are logical keys under STO-1's 0x00 namespace; the raw ledger key is 00 || 05 || be64(seq), ten bytes; then check every scan, index and canonical-length statement (STO-1/10/18/19/20/22/24/25) says which view it means. Do NOT change any byte or replace nine with ten (OVR-14). Scope the sentence 'lengths in this chapter are logical' to journal.db: in client.db STO-3's '[0x01] ++ u32_le(db_prefix), exactly five bytes' IS raw (the 0x01 is the tag). STO-5 owns the physical/logical distinction; STO-1/STO-18 cite. title: Egress rule (FMI-40) must bind every URL-hosted destination per ADR-0034: no meta_override_url fetch, private-egress host setting, link-local/metadata floor
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-10-01: the product questions are decided (`ADR-0034`, docs/adr/0034-egress-rule-binds-every-destination-private-egress-is-a-host-knob.md). This text replaces every earlier version; read the ADR first. spec-iq9 was closed into this bead.

**The gap (verified).** 02:138 (FMI-40) begins "Before any gateway request (FMI-11, and every quote or payment call to a gateway)" and refuses private, link-local, loopback and metadata destinations for gateways only; its "A host MAY offer an explicit configuration that permits private-network gateways … MUST default to off" (02:143-145) is a MAY no host can exercise under HST-2/HST-3's closed surfaces. Three classes inherit nothing: the guardian-supplied `meta_override_url` (02:402-403; the SDK's client builder spawns a meta service that GETs it every ten minutes whether or not the wallet reads it — verified at the pin: fedimint-client/src/client/builder.rs:1046, fedimint-client-module/src/meta.rs:83); the operator-configured discovery base (FMI-28) and Nostr relays (ADR-0036); and guardian HTTP/WebSocket endpoints inside invites, whoever supplied them (07:29-31 is the poisoned-feed threat).

**What ADR-0034 decided (do not re-open).**
- FMI-40 binds every URL-hosted destination: vetted-list gateway URLs, the break-glass gateway, the discovery base and relays, and every guardian HTTP/WebSocket endpoint used for preview, join, open, recovery and later use. A user-supplied invite, a Manual source, vetted-list membership and the break-glass grant NO exemption; nothing is inferred from SEC-16. iroh endpoints have no host and are out of scope.
- The wallet never fetches `meta_override_url`. FMI-26 has two shutdown inputs (the at-join authenticated config expiry and corroborated `/status`); SEC-14 and ALC-39 lose the override value and its wake; the 07 threat model's malicious-guardian item says the URL is never fetched.
- Private egress is one boolean host setting, `allow_private_egress`: a new `walletd.toml` key (HST-3) plus a standalone flag (HST-10, API-25), DEFAULT ON. While on, loopback, RFC 1918 and `fc00::/7` are reachable for every class; a FLOOR is refused regardless: `169.254.0.0/16`, `fe80::/10`, and the metadata addresses `169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200`. The MAY at 02:143-145 is replaced by this setting.
- Proxy: the rule applies to the destination the wallet resolved before CONNECT; HST-2 states the operator's obligation that the proxy connects to that destination (SEC-3's trust boundary).

**Edits.** FMI-40 rewritten as the single owner: the class list, the floor, the setting, redirects/DNS re-resolution/IPv4-mapped IPv6 extended to every class, and the refusal outcomes — a rejected gateway is unavailable; a rejected discovery base or relay is a source failure; a rejected guardian endpoint fails the preview, join, open or recovery using it. SEC-16, SEC-17, FMI-26, FMI-28, FMI-43, HST-2, HST-10 cite it; SEC-14, ALC-39 and the threat model lose the override input; HST-3 gains the key; HST-29 its parse failure. Chapter 10: one scenario per class (a guardian-listed gateway at 169.254.169.254 never contacted; a `meta_override_url` that receives no request across join, open and ten minutes of running; a feed invite with a link-local guardian endpoint rejected at join; with the setting off, a loopback gateway unavailable). The chapter-10 environment runs with the default (on). spec-tc0 extends the matrix (re-resolving DNS, IPv4-mapped IPv6, redirects).

Hand-off (done-condition 6): the reference must replace the SDK meta source (`ClientBuilder::with_meta_service`) and route gateway calls through a `LightningClientInit.gateway_conn` that enforces the rule.

Owners: FMI-40; the cited rules above. Depends on spec-6w6 (the discovery base and relay keys). spec-tc0 and spec-ee9 depend on this bead.

## PR #15 round 9 correction (2026-10-01) — additive
FMI-40 has two halves that extend differently. The ADDRESS rule (resolution, refused ranges, the connected address, IPv4-mapped forms) binds every class alike. The SCHEME rule is per class: `http`/`https` for gateways, the discovery base and HTTP guardian endpoints; `ws`/`wss` for WebSocket guardian endpoints and Nostr relays — FMI-36 requires the WebSocket transport, so applying the current http-only scheme sentence wholesale would refuse every WebSocket guardian and relay.

## PR #15 final round (2026-10-02) — supersedes the proxy clause above
ADR-0034 now PINS every proxied request to the address the wallet checked: `CONNECT` names the IP literal; a plain-HTTP request through a forward proxy names the IP with the original `Host` header. The proxy has nothing to re-resolve, so a hostname that resolves publicly at the check and to a refused address at the proxy gains nothing. HST-2's proxy row states the pinning; it no longer states an operator obligation (no proxy can meet one from a hostname alone). Scenario: through a forward proxy, a gateway hostname that re-resolves to 169.254.169.254 between check and request reaches nothing.

## Identifiers (2026-10-02)
The egress scenario is CNF-56 (the next free CNF id after spec-dgj's CNF-55): one scenario with a case per destination class. Per-contact logging of private destinations is NOT part of the decision and is not required.

title: FMI-41 / API-42 / OPS-27 conflate funding expiry with claimability; implement ADR-0037: the wallet retries a failed claim until a definitive answer
description:
BLOCKER (P0). Rewritten 2026-10-02 to consolidate every earlier section; this text replaces all of them. Read `ADR-0037` (docs/adr/0037-a-rejected-claim-is-retried-until-definitive.md) first: it records the owner's decision that the wallet retries a failed claim until a definitive answer.

**Protocol facts (verified at the pinned SDK revision and upstream master).**
1. The lnv2 server checks `expiration_or_fee` only when an incoming contract is FUNDED; claiming an existing incoming contract applies no time check. A funded, unconsumed incoming contract has no claim deadline.
2. The client's `Expired` means the contract was NEVER funded (the server returns no contract only when none exists and expiry has passed, after which funding is refused). `Expired` is reached without a claim attempt; OPS-16 already maps it; it is not a claim-retry outcome.
3. The client SDK submits the claim once, reports `Failure` when the outputs never confirm, and does not retry; a claim the client cannot build can stop the client outright. It has no re-claim entry point.

**What a receive `Failure` can mean (FMI-37's receive row: "the claim transaction was rejected … or it was accepted and note issuance then failed", position "unknown whether the incoming contract was consumed").** The states, and the decided handling:
- (a) funded and unconsumed → claimable indefinitely; the wallet keeps re-claiming.
- (b) consumed by THIS wallet, note issuance not done — "this wallet consumed it" is the wallet's own evidence: its issuance evidence holds an accepted claim transaction for the contract → ISSUANCE PENDING: not definitive; the notes are issued from that evidence, never by a second claim.
- (c) consumed by another claimant → definitively not claimable.
- uneconomical: the claim's federation fee is at least the contract's amount → definitive.

**The defects in the set.** 02:328-335 (FMI-41): a rejected claim "MUST be retried until the contract's expiry has passed" (no referent for a funded contract) and the re-claim reports "not claimable" when the contract "is expired or already consumed" (answers `not_claimable` in state (a) and (b) — funds unreachable, P0). 04:580-584 (API-42): `{key}` MUST name an operation whose contract reached "a terminal non-claim (Expired or Failed)". 03:565 (OPS-27): `Expired | Failed → Stranded`. CONTEXT.md's Incoming contract entry promises "A delayed app open does NOT forfeit an already-settled payment".

**Fix (ADR-0037 decided it; write it).**
- FMI-41 owns the rule: a receive whose claim failed stays NON-TERMINAL and keeps its inbound reservation; each reconcile pass (OPS-14's cadence) re-submits the claim with backoff (state the bound as an engineering value) until a definitive answer: claimed (receive `Done`; a move's receive leg `Settled`), not claimable — state (c) only (`Failed` with FMI-37's `receive failed:` anchor, evidence kept; a move with a settled send becomes `Stranded`), or uneconomical (`Failed` with that reason, the client not stopped). A transient failure (federation unreachable, rejected claim transaction, timeout) is never definitive. State (b) stays non-terminal with its reservation until issuance resolves — credited (`Done`) or definitively lost (`Failed`); FMI-41 names what counts as definitively lost. Drop "until the contract's expiry has passed".
- A receive in claim retry or with issuance pending is outside ALC-40's settlement-stall count and holds no OPS-6 driver-cap slot between attempts; each attempt is one perform under OPS-15.
- API-42 stays the operator's manual trigger for the same work. Its precondition widens to a receive or receive leg in claim retry or with issuance pending, as well as one that reached a terminal non-claim. Its outcomes: `claimed`, `not_claimable` (state (c) only), `uneconomical`, a transient answer, and an issuance-pending answer for state (b) — never `not_claimable` for (b). A re-claim of an already-claimed contract replays `claimed` (after a lost response the answer is `claimed`, not `not_claimable`). CNF-26 gains the precondition and an exit code for each outcome. Addressing of older attempts is spec-cuw's.
- FMI-37's receive row and OPS-16's receive map follow (word OPS-16's map as "any other final state → the receive's FMI-41 handling", so an `Uneconomical` SDK state cannot fall outside it). OPS-27: a move strands only on a definitive non-claim. HST-32 cites.
- New prohibition DEF-26 (next free DEF id; DEF-21..25 are withdrawn): an incoming contract whose claim the wallet cannot fund ends in a state and never stops the client.
- Scenarios (planted store states, the way CNF-33 and CNF-51 plant rows — an honest environment cannot reject a claim at consensus): (1) a receive in claim retry whose contract is funded and unconsumed → re-claim after the funding expiry → `claimed`, the balance rises once, the earlier failure evidence kept; the same key re-claimed again → `claimed` again (replay), balance unchanged. (2) a receive with issuance pending keeps its reservation, and a receive that would fill that room is refused. (3) a federation that keeps rejecting claims for three receives does not make the daemon exit.
- Hand-off (done-condition 6): the client SDK has no re-claim entry point; an implementation must re-submit the claim input with the operation's stored claim material.

Owners: FMI-41, FMI-37, API-42, CNF-26, OPS-16, OPS-27, ALC-40, OPS-6, DEF-26; HST-32 cites. spec-cuw depends on this bead.

comments.text:
Owner decisions (2026-10-02) on the two questions in comment 7, recorded in ADR-0037 (rewritten the same day); they supersede anything above that disagrees.

1. Pending issuance never gives up. A receive whose contract this wallet consumed but whose notes were not issued stays non-terminal, keeping its reservation, until its notes are issued (Done). No timeout, attempt count or failed retrieval ends it; nothing the wallet observes shows the notes can never be issued. There is no "definitively lost" outcome: drop it from FMI-41 and from this bead's state (b), and API-42 never answers Failed for it.

2. `reclaim` on a never-funded `Expired` receive is refused. API-42's precondition becomes an explicit list: a receive or receive leg in claim retry or with issuance pending; a receive Failed with FMI-37's `receive failed:` anchor; the receive leg of a Stranded move; a receive whose contract this wallet claimed (a replay answers `claimed`). An `Expired` receive is not eligible: 422 refused (API-6, which already lists "a reclaim of an operation that is not reclaimable"), with a fixed API-36 message (for example "incoming contract was never funded"), nothing attempted, nothing journaled, CLI exit 2 (API-28). API-36 gains that row; CNF-26 gains the case. Do not use "terminal non-claim" for the precondition: elsewhere the set's "op-terminal non-claim" includes Expired.

Evidence the three advisers checked in the SDK source: the client reaches Expired only when the server answers "no contract", which it does only when no contract exists and consensus time has passed the expiry; funding is refused against the same clock, which only advances; a consumed contract keeps its funding record, so it never reads as Expired.

title: 'trusted' move record (STO-11 validity table) and 'probed' federation (three senses) are used normatively and defined nowhere
description:
Sections below were written in up to three review rounds; where they disagree, the latest section governs.
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the second four-reviewer bead review; this text replaces the original (its "trusted" predicate rejected valid direct inflows and its "probed" fix forced two facts into one word).

**(1) "trusted" move record — used normatively, defined nowhere (verified).** 03-operation-lifecycle.md:145-147 (OPS-9) "The allocator projection weakens by move-record phase when the record is trusted"; 03:263 (OPS-45) skips pre-fund admission "when the cached move record is trusted"; 03:633 (OPS-30) "pristine (phase Created, trusted, …)"; 06:541-542 (ALC-35) "A corrupt move record falls back to the strict projection". CONTEXT.md has no entry; 05:209-239 (STO-11) has no trust rule; ADR-0024:41-43 lists "Missing, corrupt, mismatched, oversized, or impossible" but no requirement does. Trust releases reservations (Sending drops the outbound) and skips admission, so the predicate changes money admission and /v1/status.

Fix: STO-11 owns VALIDITY of a record, as a table conditional on the action and phase, from locally checkable correspondence: decodes; key equals the row key; `to`/`from`/`send_required` equal the action's (STO-11 already fixes `send_required = false` and `from = None` for a receive-only DirectInflow — so a `Settled` DirectInflow legitimately has NO `send_op`; the predicate MUST NOT require one); amount and cap transformations permitted per action; current-attempt correspondence (a record from another attempt is stale, not trusted); artifacts required vs optional per phase (Sending/Settled/Stranded need `send_op` only when `send_required`; Invoiced needs `invoice` + `recv_op`); the treatment of missing, malformed, stale and contradictory records (fallback to the strict projection). OPS-9 owns the resulting PROJECTION; OPS-30 and ALC-35 cite; OPS-45 stops using the word once spec-dgj lands (its rewrite keys on reassembled artifacts). Scenario: a valid settled direct inflow (no send_op) is trusted; a cross-attempt record is not.

**(2) "probed" federation — three senses (verified).** 06:31 (ALC-1) "whether it is probed"; 06:93 (ALC-5) "not eligible to fund, or not probed (ALC-15)" — ALC-15's `probe_gate_ok`; 06:491 (ALC-32 step 5) "exceeds the number of probed federations" and 06:615 (ALC-39) "per probed federation" — the LIGHT-probed snapshot members (every snapshot member passed the light probe); 03:476 "probed in order" is the bisection, unrelated. A successful light probe, an active-probe `Passed` verdict (ALC-25) and user approval (ALC-37) are different facts.

Fix: ALC-1 names the snapshot field by its exact predicate (ALC-37's `probe_gate_ok`, from ALC-25/ALC-37) and ALC-5 uses it verbatim; ALC-32 step 5 and ALC-39 say "snapshot federations" (a count of light-probed members is meaningful on its own — keep it as that, do not force it into `probe_gate_ok`). Never substitute route validation for active-probe qualification. Both: CONTEXT.md gains the terms citing their owners.

Owners: STO-11, OPS-9; ALC-1, ALC-5, ALC-32, ALC-39. Depends on spec-dgj (its rewrite removes one "trusted" use) and spec-j8w (which rewrites the ALC-39 sentence). Split into two beads if picked up by two agents; one agent can do both.

## Third review (2026-09-23, round 3: R1, R2, R3, R4) — where sections disagree, THIS section governs
Correction (R2, R3): 'current-attempt correspondence (a record from another attempt is stale)' is NOT locally checkable — MoveRecord (STO-11) has no attempt field. STO-11 already forbids the case by a write invariant ('written only while the intent is at the expected attempt'; 'A record write MUST NOT leave behind a record that belongs to a retired attempt'): cite that invariant instead of promising a rejection predicate, and where artifacts exist correspondence is provable through the operation log's correlation key (STO-34), which is not a local check. title: Untyped persisted fields: WatchState (STO-12), EvacuationSupersessionRecord (STO-25), FederationInfo (STO-5) break upgrade-in-place
description:
Sections below were written in up to three review rounds; where they disagree, the latest section governs.
MAJOR, promoted from the minors (R2, R3, R4; R1 keeps it minor). 05-persistence.md:241-242 (STO-12) WatchState fields carry no types: discover_backlog (bool? a count?), discover_rotation, last_discover_ms; 05:458-459 (STO-25) the sidecar fields old_attempt, refusal, old_cap_components?, … carry no types or domains; 05:83 (STO-5) FederationInfo {invite, db_prefix, joined_at (seconds)} gives no field types, and the InviteCode encoding is unstated because STO-5 says the string form appears 'only in CandidateRecord.invite' (FMI-20 contemplates an invite that does not parse). These are on-disk JSON under OVR-14's upgrade-in-place contract: two implementations can write bool against u8, or an id array against hex, and cannot read each other's stores. Fix: give every field a type, domain, optionality and STO-30 default, as STO-9, STO-15 and STO-26 do; do not claim types that are inferable elsewhere are unknown — complete the tables. Owners: STO-5, STO-12, STO-25, STO-30. (spec-nwm no longer owns FederationInfo's typing.)

## Second review (2026-09-23, four-reviewer bead review round 2: R1, R2, R3, R4)
CONFIRMED and UNDERSTATED — new LEAD item (R1, verified in the reference store): 05:242 'discover_rotation (decodes when absent as 0, the value a fresh WatchState starts at; STO-30)' and 05:533 'WatchState.discover_rotation (0)' describe an integer, but the reference store's WatchState.discover_rotation is a Vec<FederationId> (wallet-fedimint/src/journal.rs:301). A wallet written to the set writes 0 where every existing store holds an array and cannot read those stores (OVR-14), and vice versa. That is MISTYPED, not untyped. spec-60q owns the cursor/rotation semantics and lands first; this bead then fixes the bytes. Corrections to the fix: do NOT give every field a STO-30 default — STO-30 governs particular compatibility additions, not all historically required fields; state JSON representation and numeric domain, required vs nullable vs omittable, existing missing-field behaviour, defaults only where compatibility needs them, unknown-field behaviour by citation. Much is inferable and should be CITED, not re-defined: db_prefix u32 (STO-3), occurrence u64 (STO-12), discover_cursor? a FederationId (API-32 renders it), discover_backlog bool (ALC-28), the STO-25 attempts/occurrences from STO-9/DOM-16. Genuinely open: discover_rotation (above), joined_at's integer type, EvacuationSupersessionRecord fields (the reference types them as STO-25 lists, with old_cap_components: Option<EvacFeeCap>). Fold in three unfiled minors of the same class: STO-13:264-265 'every *_msat/_cap/_target/… is Msat' vs its own 'auto_join_lifetime_cap … are u32' two lines later (the explicit u32 field is a count — fix the wording); STO-5:72 'InviteCode (only in CandidateRecord.invite)' needs the sentence that FederationInfo.invite is a plain String not parsed at decode (FMI-20:104-105 relies on it; the reference stores String); OVR-14:112 '(STO-29–STO-31, which own the reference encoding)' vs STO-5:58 'this rule is the single owner of that encoding' — one owner. Include decoding examples for a valid current row, a missing required field and each supported legacy omission.

## Third review (2026-09-23, round 3: R1, R2, R3, R4) — where sections disagree, THIS section governs
Correction (R3): changing STO-12/STO-30's discover_rotation from an integer to an array needs an explicit COMPATIBILITY DISPOSITION under OVR-14 ('A persisted type changes only by gaining fields'): identify it as a correction of the specified encoding to the one every existing store already holds (Vec<FederationId>), document the accepted legacy representation, and state the treatment of a row that holds an integer (none exists in the reference; say decode failure or treat as empty). Code is evidence of what stores contain, not normative by itself — the sentence in STO-12 is what changes.

## Decisions of 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-01 (ADR-0033 to ADR-0040) — additive
ADR-0038: `FederationInfo` gains `auto_joined: bool` (written once with the registry row; decodes when absent as `true`, STO-30); spec-60q adds it, this bead types it. `joined_at` is unsigned Unix SECONDS (u64) — it now decides the weekly auto-join count, so its type and unit are load-bearing. The set is greenfield (ADR-0033): no compatibility default is owed to stores older than these rules beyond what STO-30 lists, which now includes `FederationInfo.auto_joined` (`true`) and `Policy.total_cap` (unset).

title: ALC-29 auto-join counts are undefined (decided by ADR-0038: FederationInfo.auto_joined) and ALC-28's rotation cursor is underspecified
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-10-01: the counting question is decided (`ADR-0038`, docs/adr/0038-auto-join-provenance-lives-on-the-membership.md). This text replaces every earlier version; read the ADR first. Two deliverables with separate acceptance criteria: (A) the auto-join counts, (B) the rotation cursor.

**The gap (verified).** 06:424-428 (ALC-29) gates auto-join on `lifetime ≥ auto_join_lifetime_cap`, `weekly ≥ max_auto_joins_per_week` and `concurrent_unproven ≥ 3` without defining their populations, the week boundary, or what "unproven" means. 06:403-405 (ALC-28 step 3) takes "a rotation window of max_candidates_per_pass from the stored cursor and rotation (STO-12)"; step 5 (06:419-422) already says "advance the cursor over attempted ids only; wrapped iff the window completed, auto-join completed (or stopped for budget) and the plan wrapped; backlog = !wrapped && universe non-empty".

**(A) Counts — decided by ADR-0038, do not re-open.**
- The registry row (`FederationInfo`, STO-14) gains `auto_joined: bool`, written with the row in the join's own transaction — true when auto-join created the membership, false when a user `join` (OPS-42) or a recovery (FMI-31) did — never changed afterwards; a row without the field (written by a build before it, after a rollback) decodes as `true` (STO-30, ADR-0038) — `false` would let an agent-created membership escape both caps and ALC-28's repair to `AutoJoined`.
- `lifetime` = registry rows with `auto_joined` true. `weekly` = those whose `joined_at` (Unix seconds) satisfies `now_ms − joined_at × 1000 < 604_800_000` (exactly seven days old is outside; a `joined_at` later than now is inside). A registry row that cannot be read counts once in each. Neither count reads candidate rows or the ledger, so `approve`, a lost or repaired `join:` ledger row, and a reopen (which writes no registry row) change nothing.
- `concurrent_unproven`: joined federations whose registry `auto_joined` is true and whose candidate state is not `UserApproved` and whose current active-probe verdict is not `Passed`; `approve` or a `Passed` verdict releases the slot (state this; OPS-42 already says approval does).
- Delete the sentences that made the ledger the count source: STO-22's "the auto-join caps" in its money-deciding scans, STO-35's auto-join classifier clause, OPS-42's "which is what keeps a re-open out of the auto-join counts" (a reopen writes no registry row).
- Edits: STO-14 (field, write-once), STO-5's `0x03` value, STO-30 (`FederationInfo.auto_joined` decodes when absent as `true`; its counts and CNF-18), DOM-1, API-9 (`FederationView.auto_joined`, the `list-feds` line), ALC-29 (the counts), ALC-28 step 2 (cites the field; spec-nwm writes that step). Scenario: with `auto_join_lifetime_cap` 2, a pass auto-joins A and B, the operator approves both and user-joins D; the next pass leaves C `Discovered` with `blocked_lifetime`.

**(B) Cursor — engineering, decide in the edit.** State the window's start relative to the stored cursor (first id strictly greater than the cursor, wrapping), what `discover_rotation` holds (the reference stores a `Vec<FederationId>` — a snapshot of the candidate order; spec-tj5 types it), when the rotation snapshot is refreshed, and how a candidate added or removed mid-rotation is treated. Owners: ALC-28 (selection, advancement, wrap), STO-12 (representation, with spec-tj5).

Losing the journal resets every count (accepted by ADR-0038). The 20/5/3 values are inherited defaults.

Owners: ALC-29, ALC-28, STO-14, STO-12. Depends on nothing. spec-nwm, spec-tj5 and spec-lvk depend on this bead.

title: A probe session with a no-attempt outcome is never cleared: ALC-27 needs a probe-outcome table and a separate monetary-outcome table
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the third four-reviewer bead review; this text replaces every earlier version. Where anything elsewhere disagrees with this text, this text governs.

**The defect (verified).** 06:361-367 (ALC-27): begin a session (STO-26); write the umbrella `probe:<fed>:<nonce>` row (STO-6); then preflight — "where a failure is a no-attempt that changes no verdict". 05:475-476 (STO-26): the session is "cleared in the same transaction that appends the attempt" — STO-26 defines no no-attempt cleanup transition, so a no-attempt outcome leaves the session and a non-terminal umbrella row behind. 06:763-766 (ALC-52): "retained sessions first … If any retained session is admitted this cycle only the retained group is admitted and fresh probes are deferred" — one session whose preflight keeps failing starves every fresh probe. 06:352-356 (ALC-26): `active = uncosted non-terminal umbrella rows`, "retained while active || age < 7 d" — the row reserves budget with no age limit. STO-24 never repairs `probe:` rows. The leak covers every no-attempt outcome: preflight failure; ALC-27's "Stranded, Refunded, a Failed leg IN, and an ambiguous record are umbrella-only failures that record no attempt"; DOM-21's probe/user key collision ("the probe records no attempt, as for a preflight failure"); and the crash gap between session creation and the umbrella-row write. CNF-16's "records nothing" (10:194-195) is wrong on the same facts; spec-pz6 fixes the assertion, the behaviour is decided here.

**Fix — two tables in ALC-27, kept apart.**
1. **Probe-outcome table** (verdict and lifecycle): RETAIN — 06:370-371 "a non-terminal outcome is transient and the session is retained": NO attempt is appended, the session and umbrella row stay, the verdict is unchanged; COMPLETE-WITH-ATTEMPT — the terminal write appends the attempt and clears the session (STO-26, unchanged); COMPLETE-WITHOUT-ATTEMPT — every no-attempt outcome above: in ONE nonce-fenced transaction clear the session and terminalize the umbrella row `Failed` with the reason, append no attempt, change no verdict, a stale nonce is a no-op; PREEMPT — OPS-35's "probe preempted by evacuation; no attempt recorded" is the template and joins this table. The crash gap: a session with no umbrella row is cleared at the next cycle, or the umbrella row is written in the session's own transaction — pick one.
2. **Monetary-outcome table** (what the budget release may say). ALC-27 ALREADY owns the cost formula — `cost_msat = in.amount + in.receive_fee_quoted + in.send_fee_quoted − out.amount`, "counting the in-leg only when Settled/Stranded and the out-leg only when Settled" — so do NOT write a second rule: apply that formula to every outcome, umbrella-only failures included (a preflight failure yields 0 with no leg counted; a Refunded send counts its quoted fees; a settled IN with a failed OUT counts the in-leg). What the formula does not say, and this table adds, is exposure: known spend (a settled leg's quoted fees); returned principal (a `Refunded` send still consumed its fees); outstanding exposure (a settled IN followed by a failed OUT leaves principal at the candidate; an ambiguous send failure does not establish zero cost); and WHEN ALC-26's reservation may be released — never while exposure is unknown (an uncosted terminal umbrella row with unresolved exposure keeps its reservation until the exposure is resolved or the 7-day age passes, say which). Use spec-1nc's amount vocabulary for every figure (delivered net vs credited).

No explicit retry bound is needed: once the umbrella row is terminal, ALC-52's `last_invocation` ("the newest max(created_at, updated_at) over agent Probe rows with reason ActiveProbe") already pushes the candidate's `due` to `last_invocation + retry_backoff`. STO-26, ALC-26, ALC-52 and OPS-35 cite ALC-27.

**Scenarios here:** (a) a candidate whose preflight fails twice, restart in between; a fresh probe of another candidate is then admitted, the budget shows no phantom reservation, `history` shows two `Failed` umbrella rows with the reason; (b) a terminal leg IN failed after a settled OUT — the umbrella row is `Failed` with the exposure stated and the reservation is NOT released; (c) an ambiguous send failure — same, exposure unknown.

Owner: ALC-27. Depends on spec-1nc (amount vocabulary). spec-pz6 and spec-lvk depend on this bead.

title: FMI-42 set-aside duration is 'a constant of the implementation': zero satisfies it, and any duration in seconds can expire before the selection it must bind — state the exclusion in selections
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the third four-reviewer bead review; this text replaces every earlier version (the round-2 "at least min_interval_secs" recommendation and the original "monotonic, per process" clock wording are both withdrawn). Where anything elsewhere disagrees with this text, this text governs.

**The defect (verified).** 02:209-210 (FMI-42): "A gateway that quoted and did not perform MUST be set aside … The record is not persisted, and the skip-until duration is a constant of the implementation, not a `Policy` field"; ADR-0029:139-140 "The duration is a constant with a `ponytail:` note". A zero or negligible constant satisfies the letter and recreates the livelock ADR-0029 §3 exists to stop: the same failing cheapest route wins every selection. Even a positive duration does not establish the promised behaviour: the next attempt of a `Retryable` intent is the next cycle (03:219, OPS-14: "the retry cadence is the reconcile cadence"), a cycle is "at least `min_interval_secs`, at most `base_interval_secs`" (ALC-38) with seeded values 30 s and 600 s (05:260), so a set-aside measured in seconds can expire before the selection it is meant to bind.

**Fix — state the exclusion in SELECTIONS, not seconds.** FMI-42 owns an observable exclusion contract: when it begins (the failed attempt's terminal), which selections honour it — at least the same intent's next fresh route selection and every fresh selection by any intent until then — when reconsideration is permitted (after that next fresh selection has been made, or after the pair performs elsewhere), and restart behaviour: the record "is not persisted" means it does not survive the PROCESS; a resident host carries it across cycles, a standalone invocation carries it across the selections of that one invocation and no further. Do not prescribe a clock primitive or a policy-derived duration (FMI-42 says "not a `Policy` field"). Committed-route replay (OPS-20) is untouched: a set-aside never reroutes a committed leg. The hop route's set-aside (FMI-42's route marking) uses the same contract; coordinate the wording with spec-bqv.

**Scenario here (the CNF-21 amendment is this bead's; spec-mpg repairs the CNF-21 fixture first):** a preferred route fails after quoting; a viable alternative exists; the next fresh selection for the same intent takes the alternative; a committed leg on the failed gateway still replays. Assert on the selections, not on elapsed time.

Owner: FMI-42; ADR-0029:139-140 gets a dated note. Depends on spec-mpg (CNF-21's fixture). spec-lvk no longer depends on this bead.

title: Retry re-adopts the failed attempt's raw artifacts: OPS-10 / STO-9 never clear operation_id and invoice, and OPS-18 resumes the old operation

Scenario: an expired raw receive retried mints a NEW invoice under attempt 1's correlation key; the old operation id is visible only in attempt 0's row. Owners: OPS-10, STO-9. title: FMI-11 does not say unknown keys in the routing_info body are ignored: a strict decoder treats every newer gateway as unavailable

title: Optional total balance cap (ADR-0040): Policy.total_cap, unset by default, checked by OPS-7 for receives and direct inflows
description:
MAJOR (P1). Rewritten 2026-10-01 after six bot review rounds on PR #15; this text replaces every earlier version. Read `ADR-0040` (docs/adr/0040-total-balance-cap-is-optional-and-unset-by-default.md) first: it records the decision and the three properties the check must keep; this bead owns the arithmetic that keeps them.

**Decided (ADR-0040, do not re-open).** `Policy` gains `total_cap`, an optional amount, UNSET by default (no aggregate limit, as today). When set, admitting a `Receive` or `DirectInflow` — fresh, on retry (OPS-10) and at perform time (OPS-45) — checks `aggregate + request amount ≤ total_cap`, else `over_cap`. Moves, evacuations and pays never trip it. Recovery from the seed (FMI-31) is never refused by it (OPS-7 admits recovery without arithmetic); a recovered total above the cap refuses new inflows. Lowering the cap refuses new inflows and touches nothing held. Properties: every sat once; fail closed; over-counts only refuse.

**The arithmetic, owned by OPS-7 (write it beside the per-federation check, citing OPS-9 for phases and trust).** Each item below was a real defect found in review; each needs a sentence and a scenario.
1. **Balances:** every joined federation's sampled spendable balance. OPS-45's perform-time sampling covers every joined federation when the cap is set, not only the action's endpoints.
2. **External inflows in flight:** the inbound reservations of non-terminal `Receive` and `DirectInflow` intents, a receive retrying its claim (ADR-0037) included.
3. **Internal moves in flight, counted once:** a non-terminal `Move`/`Evacuate` counts at the destination only once its send has left the source, because before that the sats are still in the source balance. Do NOT sum OPS-9's strict projection: it reserves a pending move at the destination while the source still holds it (cap 100, total 90, a pending 50 move: a 5 receive would read 145).
4. **Classify a move only after reassembly:** at OPS-28's fourth killpoint the send is committed but the cached record still reads `Invoiced` without a send operation id, while the source balance has already fallen. Reassemble from the operation log first (OPS-20, as spec-dgj does for OPS-45); a move whose state is still ambiguous after reassembly, or whose record is not trusted (OPS-9), counts at the destination — the side that refuses.
5. **Refundable pays:** a `Pay` that has funded its outgoing contract and has not reached a terminal outcome counts its amount (and the fee it would get back) in the aggregate, because a `Refunded` outcome (OPS-16) restores it; the pay's own admission is not affected.
6. **The request once:** on a retry or at perform time the request's own existing reservation is excluded before its amount is added (otherwise a receive admitted fresh can be refused on retry, and its retained reservation keeps blocking it).
7. **Fail closed:** a joined federation registered but not open (DOM-2), a failed balance read, a registry row the STO-14 listing skips as unreadable (ALC-46 keeps that poison-tolerant listing for other readers; this check must not), or an unreadable move record refuses the inflow as a transient refusal — retryable, nothing minted — never a partial sum. OPS-39 gains the reason (e.g. `total_cap_unverified`) and API-6 its status.
8. **Accepted window, state it:** an inflow credited to a balance before its intent's terminal write is counted twice until that write lands — the same window the per-federation check has; it only refuses.

**Other edits.** DOM-15 (the parameter; "twenty-eight parameters" becomes twenty-nine), STO-13 (the field, unset in the seeded row), STO-30 (decodes when absent as unset; its counts and CNF-18), API-20 and API-27 (the field and flag; their counts), CNF-26 ("each of the twenty-eight flags"). Policy validity (spec-pe4's ALC-54): a set value is positive. ALC-9 and SEC-9 already cite ADR-0040.

**Scenarios (chapter 10):** a receive that would cross the cap is refused `over_cap`, a move between the wallet's federations is admitted; a pending move does not block a receive that fits; a move at killpoint 4 is counted once; an in-flight pay that later refunds was counted, so the receive admitted meanwhile leaves the total within the cap; a receive admitted fresh is admitted again on retry; one unopened federation refuses a receive as retryable, which is admitted once it opens.

Hand-off (done-condition 6): the reference has no aggregate cap.

Owners: OPS-7 (the check and the arithmetic), OPS-9, OPS-39, OPS-45; DOM-15, STO-13, STO-30, API-20, API-27, CNF-26 align. Depends on spec-dgj (reassembly before admission). spec-ee9 depends on this bead.

## PR #15 round 9 consistency corrections (2026-10-01) — additive; the ADR governs
Item 7's refusal reasons are the ones the set already gives a failed read on the admission path: OPS-39's `storage_error` for a journal read (registry row, move record), API-36's `503 failed` for a balance read; a joined federation that is not open gets a NEW OPS-39 reason. OPS-39's storage_error row, API-37's admission-read exception and API-36's balance-read row gain the total-cap reads. A claim attempt on an already-admitted receive (ADR-0037) issues no new funding, so neither pre-fund admission nor this check runs on it.

## PR #15 round 10 correction (2026-10-01)
While any `Recover` intent is non-terminal, the balance it will add is unknown (FMI-31 rebuilds into an unregistered partition and exposes it only at the registry commit), so the total-cap check fails closed: every `Receive`/`DirectInflow` is refused as a transient refusal (retryable, nothing minted) until the recovery commits or fails. Scenario: with the cap set, a receive posted during a recovery is refused retryable and admitted afterwards if it fits.

## Owner decisions after the four-reviewer rules review (2026-10-02) — supersede anything above that disagrees
A pay that ended in FMI-37's ambiguous send `Failure` does NOT count (nothing resolves it, so counting would hold that room forever); the residual — a rare late refund carrying the total above the cap — is accepted. Inflows ARE refused while a recovery is in progress (kept).

## PR #15 final round (2026-10-02) — additive
A funded `Move` or `Evacuate` that can still be `Refunded` counts the LARGER of its possible landings until a refund is impossible: the full source refund (amount plus the fees the funding debited) or the amount delivered at the destination. Counting only the delivered amount lets a refund carry the total past the cap (100 total, a 60-unit debit for a 50-unit delivery reads 90; a 10 receive is admitted; a 60 refund makes 110). Scenario: a move that refunds after a receive was admitted leaves the total within the cap.

## Identifiers (2026-10-02)
The total-cap scenario is CNF-57; the policy validity rule that says a set `total_cap` is positive is ALC-54 (spec-pe4). The refusal reasons and inputs in item 7 belong to OPS-7 (this bead), not to ADR-0040, which states only that the check fails closed.


## PR #15 final review round (2026-10-02) — additive
- **A consistent aggregate.** The check reads balances in several federations and the operation projection at different instants, so a move that leaves its source, lands, or releases its reservation while the aggregate is assembled can fall between the samples and be counted nowhere — an inflow then passes the cap. OPS-7 MUST make the aggregate consistent with those writes: assemble it against a generation that every write which debits a source, credits a destination or releases a reservation advances, and recompute when the generation moved during assembly (or an equivalent exclusion). A recompute that cannot settle within the admission's bound refuses as transient. OPS-7's per-federation check samples `balance[to]` and the projection the same way; if it has the same gap, state the rule once in OPS-7 for both. CNF-57 gains a case: a move settling during the check never lets an inflow past the cap.
